The 800 foot ceiling allows the approach to be continued to a successful landing.
An instrument rated private pilot experienced an electrical system failure in instrument conditions. He was able to locate VFR conditions and continued to his destination.
EMB-145 Captain reports being vectored to a visual approach inside the FAF and too close to a heavy jet during a night approach to MEM.
show: 2014-09 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Final Approach

text: B737 Captain believes that the practice by PHL Tower of departing aircraft simultaneously of Runway 9L and 8 is unsafe.

Dispatcher believes that the Dispatch Manager is operating outside of company policy when he instructs an operations agent to push back a flight during a thunderstorm because the crew is about to go illegal.
B737-700 Dispatcher reports not noting a NOTAMed airspace closure and files the standard route. This results in a reroute by ATC and landing with less than planned fuel.
CRJ-200 First Officer reported deviating from cleared course on approach to CLT; citing multiple runway changes and slow FMC processor speed as contributory.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: EMB-145 Captain reported track deviation on approach to DFW; citing late ATC runway change as contributory.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: DA-2000 flight crew reported confusion interpreting the OKC TRUPR1 RNAV departure and pushed over at 700 AGL triggering a GPWS alert.
B737-800 flight crew received a GPWS 'Obstacle' warning when they deviated from charted procedure on a night visual approach to LGA.
A300 Captain reported flying into convective area with moderate to severe turbulence that was not painted by his weather radar.
A300 flight crew reported a main gear tire exploded in cruise at FL320 causing damage to the wheel well door.
B737-700 Flight Attendant reported several passengers became ill from a foul odor in the cabin that appeared to be coming from the forward lav area.

An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) informs his company Engineering that a Job Card for pulling specific Circuit Breakers for #1 Engine on A321 aircraft actually has #2 Engine typed in the header of the Job Card. Not only were safety concerns raised; but also the lack of awareness by technicians who have been signing-off for work accomplished on a Job Card with an incorrect engine position.
RV-7 pilot continued VFR flight into worsening weather until becoming VFR On Top then descended through the overcast based on GPS position and was able to land in VMC.
Controller describes a situation where the aircraft is VFR on top and declares an emergency.  The aircraft is never given an altitude to maintain or a clearance for a visual approach to the airport.
B757 flight crew reported crossing BYSUN high after runway assignment was changed three times on arrival to IAH.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Final Approach

text: A300 flight crew reports being dispatched with the number two generator inoperative and the APU running. On the first two legs momentary ECAM messages are noted but quickly clear on their own. On the final leg during descent; multiple ECAM messages appear with some remaining and others self clear. The First Officer's flight displays and ECAM screen blank momentarily and the autopilot and yaw dampers disengage. An emergency is declared and a normal landing ensues; with no anomalies during the last ten minutes of flight.
CE-560XL flight crew reported ACM Overheat light illuminated on climb out; accompanied by smoke and odor. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: B737 flight crew report receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on approach to OAK after misunderstanding altitude clearance.

B757 flight crew experiences a pack failure during takeoff that initially results in very high air flow and high temperatures. The left pack is placed in the standby cold position which seems to correct the problem. The flight attendants report damage to the side wall in the cabin and agitated passengers. The Captain investigates and finding the damage to be significant; elects to return to the departure airport.
CRJ-900 flight crew reported deviating from charted altitude on arrival to MEM; citing confusion regarding runway assignment.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: An SR20 flight instructor and student suffered an NMAC with a King Air while on a training flight.

A day after having performed a previously approved stadium overflight demonstration with nine homebuilt aircraft the pilots received notice through a third party (an association officer) dated prior to the event advising any such flights would be in violation of CFR 91.319c.

C150 pilot reports losing track of the C172 ahead in the traffic pattern and turning crosswind too early resulting in a NMAC. The Tower called out the potential conflict and both pilots took evasive action. The C172 pilot's report is also included.
C208 pilot reported an NMAC with another light single on approach to ICT when he lost sight of slower traffic he was following.

ATL Local Controller described a conflict between two air carrier aircraft when an Embraer cleared to fly a visual to Runway 28 failed to turn in a timely fashion and threatened a widebody aircraft established on final for Runway 27L.
Local Controller described a go-around event caused by his/her misidentification of two like aircraft in the pattern; radio communications adding to the confusion.
Enroute controller reported a possible loss of separation but only after the suspected conflict was identified after a reviewed on the FALCON replay system.
P50 Departure Controller reports of a PHX departing aircraft on the incorrect SID which was sent via the PDC.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: B737NG Captain reported loss of TAT probe resulted in multiple confusing system errors.
B737 Captain describes a runway change during the SEAVU 2 arrival to LAX that results in some altitude and track deviations when the FMC is switched from 24R to runway 25L.
An air carrier Captain; on downwind for landing at ORF; observed an apparent unmanned aerial vehicle some 200' below and 1/4NM to the left of their flight.
Q400 Captain on an ILS for the right runway experiences a NMAC with a C208 on a visual approach for the left runway. A TCAS TA is annunciated and the Q400 Captain descends visually to avoid the C208.

An EMB-135 Captain; in the landing flare for runway 31R at JFK; believes his aircraft was buffeted by the jet blast of an aircraft cleared for an intersection takeoff from runway 22R.  The reporter was able to recover from the upset and land safely in a left crosswind although touching down first on the downwind right main landing gear.

B737 flight crew experiences pressurization failure after takeoff on a ferry flight with eight empty pallets stacked on top of each other in the number nine position. The short flight is continued to destination at 10;000 feet. Post flight reveals that the pallets had broken lose and punctured the aft pressure bulkhead.

Flight crew experiences a right wing down rolling tendency as the aircraft accelerates to 250 knots after takeoff requiring 3.5 units of left wing down aileron trim. The aircraft had a history of similar flight control issues and the crew elects to return to the departure airport.

BE76 instructor pilot reports sighting a small blue flame coming from underneath the right engine; near the cowl flap during descent. The flame appeared to get worse so the engine is shut down; and an emergency is declared.

Large Cargo aircraft flight crew experiences a sudden pitch over while being vectored for arrival and using VNAV for the descent path. The pitch over occurred just after a waypoint; with a charted holding pattern and located behind the aircraft; was removed from the legs page of the FMC. The autopilot is quickly disconnected and the aircraft returned to a reasonable descent rate and airspeed.

After encountering an intermittent gear unsafe light (after landing); the flight crew of a DHC-8 agreed to ferry the aircraft for maintenance. On that approach; the nose gear failed to remain extended. They conducted the alternate gear extension abnormal check list successfully; and landed without further incident.

B737-800 Captain reports being cleared to land Runway 35L at DFW. At the FAF the landing runway is changed to 35R which the Captain does not accept and the runway is changed back to 35L. The Captain cites the runway length and the one mile sidestep required as reasons for not accepting the runway change. The Ground Controller provides a telephone number to call.
show: 2014-10 · ATC Issue All Types · Final Approach

text: MD-83 flight crew experiences a track deviation during the FORCK 1 RNAV departure from Runway 35L at DFW. With the autopilot engaged the aircraft begin a turn to the east prior to reaching MECHL. The early turn is detected by ATC and a vector heading is provided.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Air Carrier Captain reports loss of GPS information during approach to Runway 5L at MMMX. Unsafe gear also occurs later in the approach resulting in a go-around.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: C414 pilot reports an inadvertent entry into into a TFR. The reporter was using a Foreflight cell phone application to display TFR's; but a previous adjustment to the display intensity rendered the TFR boundary invisible.

CE550 Captain experiences track and altitude deviation during a maintenance test flight after scheduled inspections and the installation of an overhauled GPS and Multi-Function Display unit. The GPS antenna was found damaged on post flight.

Two aircraft; occupied by student pilots and instructors; experienced a near-mid-air-collision when the faster trailing aircraft pilots did not observe the slower leading aircraft; and turned crosswind towards them.
Pilot reports a loss of communication with ATC in a specified area of Texas. Pilot finds correct frequency and changes to the new frequency.

SR22 pilot believes he may have entered a firefighting TFR while on base and final for Runway 25 at AUN. The existence of the TFR was confirmed with FSS but the TFR would not display on the aircraft MFD.

CE560 Captain reports a track deviation departing CVG due to confusion over a similar sounding fix names. The clearance was V128 YRK RHODE as filed; but ROHDE was entered in the FMC instead of RHODE. ATC detects the error.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: Small aircraft instructor reports conflicts with with wildlife departing Runway 21 at JNX and suggests that something needs to be done to reduce the problem.

Flight crew describes a flight to DAL with four routing and arrival changes after becoming airborne. Enroute at FL400 a descent clearance is issued by ATC and accepted by the crew; but passing FL388 ATC states that the crew must have accepted someone else's clearance and to climb back to FL400.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: A Citation Captain departing HWD on Runway 28L describes a conflict with a B737 arriving OAK on the ILS 30. A description of the event from the perspective of the two B737 pilots is also included. The B737 First Officer questions the wisdom of allowing left turn out departures from HWD with traffic on the ILS 30 to OAK.
PA34 pilot reported he deviated from charted procedure on a steep approach to FDK in IMC that resulted in a CFTT incident.
A pilot and flight instructor experienced a right main landing gear collapse during landing rollout.
TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event claiming the introduction of OAPM airspace as well as some current procedures contributed to the incident.
TRACON Controller providing OJT described an airspace incursion when the FLM directed an alternate plan of action differing from the intentions of the controllers working the position.
Enroute Controller described a probable airspace infraction when utilizing the long established AIT procedure.
Enroute Controller described an automated hand off problem when the data did not transfer to the receiving controller as expected.
B737-700 Captain reported losing contact with ATC when they incorrectly entered a new frequency. Situation was complicated by a wake turbulence encounter.
show: 2014-10 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: B737-700 Flight Crew reports being cleared for the ILS 24R off the RIIVR 2 to LAX. Before intercepting the LOC for 24R; ATC cancels the clearance and tells the crew to turn left and intercept the LOC for the ILS 25L; and that the original clearance had been to 25L.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: First Officer reports being struck by lightning during initial climb; resulting in three of the four main display panels going blank. Attempts to restore the lost panels are not successful and the flight returns to the departure airport after dumping fuel.

When the B737 flight crew; cleared to 'descend via' the DRLLR RNAV STAR to IAH; requested their planned landing runway so as to properly program the FAA required 'bottom' altitude in the arrival ATC's response was that assigning a landing runway was not his responsibility; the next controller would make the assignment and advising he was weary of having to explain that to flight crews.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: CRJ-200 flight crew reports attempting to depart DCA with an incorrect flap setting after changing to a full thrust takeoff due to gusty winds. Flaps were set to 20 for the reduced thrust takeoff and should have been set to 8 for the full thrust takeoff. When the error is detected during the takeoff the Captain rejects at 90 knots.

Air carrier Captain reports being cleared for the ILS Y Rwy 02 from AUR just after another carrier is cleared for the ILS Z 02 at MGGT. This results in the reporter turning from the southwest to intercept the localizer while the other aircraft is turning from the south to intercept the same localizer. A TCAS RA results and the Captain climbs in compliance with the RA and is vectored for another approach by a different Controller.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: When their MD-83; which had been delivered from Maintenance right at departure time; failed to pressurize the flight crew returned to their departure airport.  On the return they noted that the cabin altitude control lever had been left in the manual position; possibly by Maintenance personnel.  In their haste to depart it had been overlooked.
B737-800 Captain reports not detecting a SID change in the PDC; resulting in a track deviation on departure. ATC quickly detects and corrects the error.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Following announcing the approach on the CTAF frequency; a PA28 pilot discovered a stationary helicopter occupying the runway during rollout. He was able to avoid a collision only to hear first communication from the helicopter reporting hovertaxi off the runway.

A flight instructor and student flying a practice VOR RWY 30 approach at LGB suffered an NMAC with pattern traffic when the transmission and receipt/execution of a go-around clearance from ATC was not accomplished in a timely fashion.
Pilot reports of a loss of communication with ATC in a known dead spot for radio communication.
Helicopter pilot reported an NMAC with a Cessna at PRC airport when he misunderstood his taxi clearance.
MD-82 Captain reported receiving a Resolution Advisory (RA) on a 'descend via' clearance; citing workload in the old technology transports as interfering with their traffic scan.
CRJ-200 First Officer reported loss of cabin pressure after they were dispatched with one pack inoperative; and the remaining pack failed at FL250.

A flight attendant aboard a B757-200 reported the passenger agent; despite several reminders it was inappropriate; closed the cabin door while passengers were still in the aisle and approximately half of the overhead bins were still open in violation of SOP and FARs.
An Bonanza 36 pilot reported flying a VOR approach using a NOTAMed out of service VOR. Reporter cited the poor formatting and presentation of NOTAMs as contributory.
show: 2014-10 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: A319 flight crew experiences ECAM's for Captain's pitot and engine 1 reverser unlocked at rotation. Many autoflight functions are not available and the crew elects to return to the departure airport. With the ILS OTS the RNAV is chosen but cannot be loaded in the FMGC. The VOR approach is then chosen and tuned on the RMP's. After landing a landing gear disagree ECAM is displayed.
A320 Captain described ramp personnel encouraging what he felt were dangerous deviations from SOPs at IAH.
BE-400XP Captain reported smoke and odor coming from his First Officer's iPad charge cord while it was connected the USB charging port.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: MD-80 Captain reported struggling to get the FMS re-programmed after a late runway change from ATC. Reporter recommended ATC stick with the original clearance and minimize short-notice changes.

An A319 flight crew was expecting the ILS to Runway 6R at CLE due to the ATIS information and a NOTAM closing Runway 6L. Upon check in with Approach they are advised that a new ATIS is current and to intercept the localizer. The next clearance is for the ILS 6L which the crew is not ready for but manages to set up and execute.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: A Mcdonnell Douglas widebody flight crew experienced a stick shaker and SLAS DISAG alert as the aircraft was slowed through 150 KTS during approach. A go-around is initiated and a second approach with higher Vspeeds results in the same alerts and another go-around. The next approach is accomplished with the slats retracted to a successful landing.

MQ9 pilot reports turning the aircraft around to return to base; when the original mission is canceled due to weather. When the operational mission in the aircraft was updated; the aircraft started a turn back to the south. This was quickly detected by the pilot and corrected manually.
show: 2014-09 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: ACY TRACON Controller describes an aircraft that descends below the FAF altitude to the minimum descent altitude causing a low altitude alert. The aircraft is advised of the low altitude and then sees the airport and lands safely.
LGA controllers describe a runway incursion due to the Local Controller forgetting that he/she had approved a runway crossing downfield.
M03 Approach Controller reports of turning aircraft to final and losing the required separation with another aircraft on the opposite base leg.

Air carrier flight crew notes a bird pass under their aircraft as they climb off Runway 25R at LAX. The flight continues to destination after ATC informs them that a hawk was found on the runway but no anomalies were detected aboard the aircraft. Post flight reveals a dent in the right engine cowling.

An air carrier baggage handler reported difficulties loading an electric wheelchair in the cargo pit of a CRJ-700 citing excessive weight for handling without mechanical assistance; the inability to load it 'upright' (which he believes to be contrary to regulation) and the need to do so with the side rails of the loader down to accommodate its bulk thus exposing handlers to falls and the possibility of the 300 pound chair falling and; perhaps; crushing handler who fell beneath it.

B717 fight crew reports forgetting to shut down the right engine after gate arrival then departing separately to obtain lunch. The First Officer returns first and is informed the right engine is still running; which is shut down.

F2TH Captain experiences a baggage compartment fire warning climbing through FL280. The First Officer is sent back to investigate and can find no fire but there is some faint smoke and temperatures seem to be elevated. The Baggage Fire Checklist directs the crew to disable the baggage fire warning if there is no actual fire present and continue. The crew elects not to do this and diverts in a non emergency fashion.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: MD83 flight crew experiences a burnt rubber smell shortly after takeoff which is confirmed by the flight attendants in the rear of the aircraft along with an unusual vibration. While discussing the issue the right engine begins compressor stalling. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing with the right engine at idle.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: B757-200 Captain reported diverting to a suitable airport after a utility buss began generating an electrical burning smell.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: BE-36 pilot reported his throttle cable came loose leaving the engine at full power. Pilot proceeded to a nearby airport where he shut down the engine and landed dead stick.

An MD-83 flight crew got confusing NAV information between their FMS and VOR based systems. They opted to continue to destination utilizing the VOR. Approaching their destination they received CAS messages reflecting FMS and NAV buss problems. Upon recycling power to the FMC post landing the fault messages cleared. They wrote up the event in the logbook.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: PA18 Instructor describes a night cross country flight with a student during which weather and a hand held GPS unit conspire to produce a Class C airspace incursion.
C310 pilot reported his right main gear separated from the aircraft on landing roll out. Three greens were confirmed before landing.
ABQ Tower Controller and pilot describe a loss of separation with an aircraft on the runway and one landing over the top of the aircraft on the runway.
B737-300 flight crew reported noticing strong electrical fumes and electrical system anomalies during taxi. They returned to the gate for maintenance.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Taxi
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A320 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff at 80 knots when ATC reported a truck on the runway. During the stop the aircraft pulled to the left and smoke was observed; so they returned to the gate for maintenance attention.
HS-125-900XP Captain reported encountering multiple fuel leak issues over the last few months in the Hawker fleet that he feels are not being properly addressed by Maintenance.
B747-400 international first officers reported the pilot flying descended below charted altitude at FAF on RNAV approach to SBEG while using FLCH rather than VNAV.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: B737-800 flight crew reports being cleared for takeoff by the Tower then; at 100 knots; commanded to abort. The Tower Controller apparently perceived that a DC-10 was about to enter the runway down field.

B767-300ER international flight crew reported they failed to select final flaps in a timely manner creating an unstabilized approach scenario; and they then failed to execute a go-around. Fatigue was cited as a factor by the pilot flying.

Captain describes his efforts to have his company Maintenance Control direct a Contract Maintenance provider to troubleshoot the cause of his left EHSI and RMI showing a heading of 085 compared to the right EHSI of 175 degrees that matched the Magnetic compass and aircraft orientation. Maintenance flashlight found in the left wing Flux Valve access area of the Pilatus PC-12 aircraft. Issue of Tool Control also raised.
Air carrier Dispatcher reported operational control issues related to insufficient staffing.
B757-200 flight crew reported abnormal rudder trim reactions that led to a return to departure airport.
EMB-145LR First Officer reported getting a terrain advisory from GPWS in the pattern at TYS.
PC-12 Captain reported stick shaker activation just after takeoff possibly related to AOA anomalies.
B737 First Officer reported departing with fuel out of balance; citing a number of distractions as contributory.

While troubleshooting; a flight crew reports that the ailerons felt 'nowhere near normal and were very sloppy when flown by hand.' An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) finds the aft attach hardware for the roll Artificial Feel Unit (AFU); had fallen out due to the pin not being safe-tied. The roll Aileron Trim actuator was also; not properly safe-tied. The Dassault Falcon DA-2000 Maintenance Manual (M/M) instructs Maintenance 'not' to safety attaching hardware until rigging is completed.
AC90 pilot reported a nose gear tire failed after landing; resulting in a fire in the nose gear area.
show: 2014-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Landing
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Light aircraft pilot reported NMAC with another light aircraft on departure from LCI.
B200 pilot reported he had to brake 'abruptly' to avoid a collision with another aircraft on a taxiway he was cleared to join; at ADS. It is unclear if this is a pilot or ATC error.

Pilot of a Bellanca Super Viking B17-31 aircraft describes his efforts to verify all three landing gears were extended using Manual Extension procedures and fly-bys of a local tower; after the gears failed to retract following takeoff. Maintenance identified one of several O-rings in a Gerdes Control Valve that allowed hydraulic pressure to occur simultaneously on both; the return and pressure side of the landing gear's hydraulic system.
EC135 pilot reported an NMAC with a crop duster on initial lift-off. Reporter stated he felt the crop duster was not complying with appropriate procedures.
The pilot of a PA31 was surprised by an unusual attitude while on an IFR flight plan when the autopilot became unexpectedly disconnected.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: While attempting to land at a private airport; the pilot of an experimental aircraft was unable to stop on the usable runway. Fearing a conflict with overhead aircraft if a go-around was attempted; the pilot ran off the end of the runway and into a pond.
The pilot of a Cessna 425 experienced a gear up landing following an approach in which the gear warning horn was reported to not have sounded.

PC12 pilot reports receiving an IFR departure clearance from 7B2 departing Runway 14 to turn right after takeoff on a southwesterly heading. The reporter questions the turn direction as being opposite to the VFR pattern and notes that he came dangerously close to terrain before starting his turn above traffic pattern altitude.

Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) were informed that an MD-88 aircraft they had just performed an 'M' procedure for an MEL deferral of the Right Engine Fuel/Oil Heat Valve; had developed uncontrollable high fuel and oil temperatures on climbout; requiring an inflight engine shutdown. Valve had been physically positioned to the 'closed' position; but not safety wired and vibrated to the 'open' position after engine start-up.

ISP Controller and pilots involved describe a situation where an aircraft is cleared for takeoff and another aircraft with clearance crosses the runway down field. The departing aircraft aborts takeoff.

B737-300 flight crew reports exceeding 250 knots below 10000 feet when ATC deletes a crossing restriction on the POMONA7 SID and the crew dials in the new assigned altitude on the MCP but forgets to delete the restriction in the FMC. The aircraft attempts to level off for the restriction and accelerate above 250 knots due to inoperative auto thrust.
B777 Captain expressed concern about the design of the iPad mount; stating it interferes with other components.
A320 Series Captain reported receiving an erroneous GPWS terrain warning on approach to PDX Runway 28L. Controller reportedly stated that this was a known Airbus issue.
B737-800 flight crew reported descending below charted altitude on night visual approach to LAX.

A Flight Attendant and the two pilots involved describe a rough landing caused by the failure of both tires on the right main gear; also causing brake failure. The two tires in question had been replaced by maintenance two flights previous to the incident flight (second landing).
show: 2014-10 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: Military helicopter pilot describes a conflict that develops with a air carrier on approach to HNL; when the reporter anticipates a clearance from the Tower that is not delivered as expected.

PA34 pilot reports a NMAC with a glider during approach to Runway 23 at ZPH; while the glider was apparently on approach to Runway 19. Runway 23 was the wind favored runway while Runway 19/1 was being used by jump aircraft and gliders and both left and right hand traffic patterns.

C172 Instructor describes a loss of control incident after a bounced landing by his student during which the instructor took control. A runway excursion occurs resulting in damage to the aircraft after contact with a hangar.
B737 flight crew receiving bad takeoff data during a rushed departure; resulting in low V speeds and an improper trim setting. The aircraft feels sluggish to the First Officer during rotation.
Air Carrier First Officer at FL310 reports being routed a little too close to a rocket launch that explodes just after lift off.
A C-208 Captain reported physical symptoms following TKS anti-ice spray bar fluid dispensing. A windshield air leak suspected.
McDonnell Douglas widebody flight crew reports being confused by the altitudes depicted on the Quiet Bridge Visual approach and whether they are manditory or recomended.
show: 2014-10 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Initial Approach
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: PA31 pilot reports that the nose wheel scissors pin is removed for towing and the scissors reconnected afterwards but the pin is not reinstalled. This is not detected during preflight and the aircraft is taxied out for departure. As the weight comes of the nose wheel during takeoff a shudder develops and the nose gear does not retract. The gear is cycled with the same result. Upon returning to the departure airport the nose gear will not extend and is pumped down. A successful landing ensues with both engines shut down during the roll out.
BE200 flight crew describes the cause of a descent below minimums during a LP GPS approach. A low altitude alert is issued by the Tower.

The pilot of a high performance aerobatic aircraft is informed of an airborne conflict after landing by the pilot of the C182 involved. The reporter was flying a non standard pattern at higher speed and closer in due to the performance characteristics of his aircraft.
Instructor pilot doesn't see that student has wrong frequency selected and aircraft enters runway and aircraft goes around because student had selected another Tower's frequency.

M20 pilot experiences three go-arounds due to his inability to get the aircraft to slow to landing speed. On the fourth attempt the mixture is pulled on short final and a normal landing ensues. The throttle cable was found disconnected from the fuel control lever.
SDF Approach Controller has a loss of separation when an aircraft on final over takes another.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Final Approach

text: Tower describes a situation where he is talking to a helicopter and in lands off the airport in an emergency situation.

LHD and MRI Controller's report of an aircraft at MRI airport on the ground; talking to LHD Controller's asking for takeoff clearance. LHD Controller clears aircraft for takeoff and at MRI the Controller sends an aircraft around because the aircraft was close to the runway.
ZHU Controller describes problems with various aircraft inbound to IAH that are not clear with a NOTAM that has speed restrictions on it that relate to a STAR for IAH.
CRJ-200 First Officer reported wake encounter departing ATL in trail of an MD-80 that resulted in two low altitude 20-degree rolls.
A320 Captain reports not noting the fact that the JAGUAR4 Departure from MCO has a second page containing the initial climb and routing information.

While preparing for the before start checklist; a B737 Captain reports only turning on one center tank fuel pump. This is not detected by either pilot during the checklist and the flight departs in that condition. An impending fuel imbalance is detected during climb and several minutes pass before the cause is detected and corrected.

B737 flight crew reports landing with a flap setting of 25 due to strong gusty winds which is contrary to the company's authorized landing flap settings. Low time for both pilots in the aircraft; ATC issues and weather were cited as factors in the incident.
A321 flight crew reported three wake encounters on climbout in trail of a B777-200 that induced roll and prompted the crew to deviate from the assigned course.

Cessna pilot reports a NMAC in the traffic pattern at APA requiring evasive action. The traffic landing ahead of the reporter does not clear the runway after landing requiring a go-around. The traffic on the runway; the traffic for the parallel runway and the traffic for the crossing runway were all cited as conflicts during the go-around.
C182 pilot; on takeoff roll; sights a PC12 entering the runway down field and rejects the takeoff. No reports had been heard on the CTAF from the PC12 pilot; but he did apologize after the incident.

After being issued a descend via the ENDEE 3 except maintain 11;000; a CE560 Captain is issued a Runway 31C transition via GAGGA by Approach. Without the altitude being mentioned or modified the Captain levels at 11;000 FT and is queried by ATC as to why.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: ZSE controller reports of an aircraft that is cleared for an approach but descends below the MEA.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: HCF TMU Controller reports failing to note the active status of W-188 until queried by another Controller about a target at FL350 in the Warning Area. PMRF is contacted and the target is identified as a UAV. Multiple faxes from PMRF changing the active times resulted in the oversight.
ERJ170 flight crew; distracted by a concern for clearing the gate for an incoming aircraft; failed to contact Ground Control prior to commencing taxi.
A321 First Officer experiences the failure of the Blue hydraulic pump during climb passing FL240. After consultation with the company the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport.

'Descending via' the KLNDR RNAV STAR to DFW without benefit of autoflight NVAV capability the flight crew of an E145 descended through the required 11;000 FT prior to DIETZ and received a TCAS TA and an alert from ATC to return to 11;000 FT.  The lack of autoflight VNAV capability; and the non-user-friendly location of the single FMS control head were cited as contributing factors.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: E145 Captain describes a test of wills between the gate agent and himself when the gate agent is instructed not to board until a new flight attendant arrives at the aircraft. The aircraft is boarded without the cockpit crew present and with no power on the aircraft.
B737 flight crew reports a near ground collision with van that fails to yield during taxi out from the gate.

CRJ700 flight crew reports being asked by ATC for their best rate to FL350; then being distracted by minor tasks that allow the aircraft to slow to 180 knots and sticker activation. A text book recovery is performed.

C210 pilot experiences flashing runway edge and centerline lights during a night visual approach to Runway 26R at ATL. When propeller RPM is varied the strobe effect is varied and it is decided that the effect is caused by propeller interaction with the LED lights which are apparently flashing at a high rate.

Instructor pilot reports electing to enter clouds without a clearance due to unexpectedly low ceilings while on a VFR flight. A clearance is quickly obtained from Approach Control and the instructor and student continue to destination.

A student pilot had difficulty understanding ATC instructions and mis-identified the aircraft he was to follow. His early turn led to a traffic conflict that was separated by ATC. The current and former flight instructors provided similar accounts and suggestions.
Stearman pilot lost control of his aircraft when he encountered a tailwind gust during landing; resulting in a ground loop and slight wing tip damage.
JAX Controllers report of a runway incursion by an airport vehicle with an aircraft on final that goes around due to the vehicle's position.
An A320 flight crew had a close encounter with a UAV they identified as a red; white and blue model aircraft operating above 10;000 FT; within the confines of and at or above the MCO Class B.
B737-400 Captain detects very sluggish takeoff performance and suspects that the takeoff data they received did not reflect the actual aircraft load.

Hawker 850 flight crew describes a rejected takeoff that results after the Captain begins having directional control issues at 60 knots. Post flight revealed that the right nose tire had come off its bead.
show: 2014-10 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: B737-900 flight crew reported slower than normal acceleration on takeoff roll; possibly resulting from autothrottle malfunction or error in weight and balance calculations. Captain added power at rotation to assure obstacle clearance.
Flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from the tower on a night visual approach to TUS runway 11L.
A Captain reports two similar sounding fix names used by PCT with the HYPER 5 arrival resulted in a track deviation. The reported fixes are CEEVE and SIGBE.
show: 2014-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: A glider pilot inadvertently entered restricted airspace and experienced a near-mid-air-collision with a high performance military aircraft. The lack of a transponder may not have allowed ATC to recognize that the pilot was off the expected route.

The pilot of a small aircraft landing at a non-towered airport; observed the aircraft ahead land on the grass alongside the runway; then taxi across the runway unannounced. The landing aircraft was forced to take evasive action to avoid a ground collision.
The pilot of a V35 Bonanza experienced engine power problems and diverted to a nearby airport. A loose fuel line was identified as the problem.
The pilot of a multi-engine aircraft became aware of another aircraft in close proximity; and took evasive action. ATC was unaware of any traffic in the area; and was unable to identify any on radar.
show: 2014-09 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: B737-800 flight crew experiences a TCAS TA and EGPWS cautions and warnings while on a night visual approach. The First Officer makes adjustments to the glide path to silence the warnings although no actual deviations below the glidepath are detected and the approach is continued to landing. The aircraft had been written-up for lightning strikes recently.

After being issued a speed restriction by ATC along with the advice; 'Expect short approach;' B737-700 flight crew slowed below assigned speed due to their high; in close position. ATC advised of a possible violation.

B757 First Officer discovers during takeoff that auto thrust is inoperative during the takeoff. The takeoff is continued and in cruise it is discovered that maintenance pulled the wrong circuit breaker while attempting to comply with an MEL procedure for the left autopilot.

A Dispatcher lost contact with a long range flight on a polar route; missing real time position reports at three fixes (later received) and was unable to communicate the re-dispatch message as required.

DHC8-100 Captain experiences a lightning strike in cruise resulting in the loss of both DC generators and both VOR's. The generators are successfully reset but the VOR's are not and the flight diverts to a VFR airport.

Flight Dispatcher reports being unable to contact a crew to inform them that their next flight is canceled. ATC is contacted and the filed flight plan is canceled. The crew manages to get around this obstacle and depart on time.

A Captain was informed he had flown a CRJ-200 aircraft with the Right nose wheel tire improperly installed. The chine (tire ring) was found facing inward instead of outward. Pilot noted certain factors may have contributed to the missed chine position that included the aircraft was already delayed; time pressure to get back on schedule and the aircraft tug was already connected to the nose gear.

Upon takeoff the Captain of an EMB-175 found it necessary to maintain full down elevator deflection to prevent over rotation. The condition continued until flight attendants were able to move passengers forward. The Captain recalled noting the trim set at 4.8 units ANU during preflight and the First Officer noted 10.1 ANU during the struggle to maintain a safe attitude.
A319 First Officer reported encountering wake on arrival to DFW in 10-mile trail of an A380 that resulted in a 25-degree bank.
CRJ-700 flight crew reports entering an incorrect holding pattern at SKARF due to misunderstanding the clearance and the way the arrival chart is laid out.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: Private pilot reports inadvertently entering IMC at 2500 feet. ATC is contacted and provides assistance resulting in a safe landing.
Without informing ATC; B737-700 flight crew slowed below last assigned speed in order to descend fully configured in a stabilized approach.

When the flight crew of a B737-NG negotiated a more neighborly RNAV SID for departure from DAL with Clearance Delivery their Departure Controller was apparently not informed and asked the crew which of DAL's 22 SIDs they were on after giving them a 'direct to' clearance on course. When advised they were on the KRUMM the Controller verbally shook his head stating '...I just can't keep track of them all.'
show: 2014-11 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: B737-700 Captain describes FMC anomalies that occur when changing from the RNAV X RWY 22L to the RNAV Y RWY 22L approaching MIING on the ENDEE3 arrival to MDW. This change results in the entire ENDEE3 arrival being entered into the FMC and creates a route discontinuity after MIING.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: A Contract Mechanic was directed by Maintenance Control to pressurize the cabin of an EMB-145 aircraft to below sea level in the manual mode. Flight crew and Flight Attendant were not made aware after being requested to start engines with the main cabin door closed. Uncomfortable ear pressure was experienced. Crew departed in the morning; but pressurization and flight at altitude may not have been advisable due to scuba dive effect.
A B737-NG First Officer reported sighting a UAV within 400 FT of their flight path as they climbed through 4;000-4;500 MSL south and west of DFW on the HRPER1 SID.

CRJ-200 Captain reports inadvertently fueling with the main cabin door closed. After engine start; a PA28 is heard on the CTAF to be taxiing for takeoff. Upon reaching the parallel taxiway the PA28 is seen to be accelerating down the taxiway; and lifts off very close to the CRJ.
Pilot reports entering Los Angeles class bravo airspace without clearance; while under flight following.

PA28 instructor; with student flying a GPS approach under simulated partial panel conditions; reports allowing his student to drift off course into the approach path of the parallel runway; consequently causing a NMAC with a Bonanza. The Bonanza pilot asks the Tower what the PA28 is doing; alerting the instructor to the deviation.

C310 pilot discovers that his aircraft has lost all electrical power when the gear will not retract after takeoff. Unicom is contacted via cell phone and the first approach results in a go-around when the flaps cannot be extended. The second approach is planned with no flaps and ends successfully.

C210 pilot experiences icing conditions at 9;000 feet with no ability to descend due to a MVA of 8;500 feet. With the icing becoming excessive; pilot stresses urgency to ATC and a descent to 8;000 feet results in VMC and temperatures above freezing.
AGS FLM reports of an ALTRV that no one was briefed on.  The controllers were unfamiliar with an ALTRV and apparently have never worked one before.
Arrival Controllers describe situation of a configuration change that didn't go smoothly resulting in a loss of separation with an opposite direction arrival.

Arriving into IAH off the HKORY1; B737 flight crew is issued a runway change from Runway 9 to Runway 8R. The crew makes an incorrect assumption that this runway requires a north transition over DOMNO. The routing note describing the route for each runway is missed when the iPad is zoomed in.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: An EMB-170 flight crew inbound to DFW filed for; set up and briefed to descend via the JOVEM RNAV STAR; IBAKE transition was given two STAR changes during their descent; first to descend via the DEBBB then; as they approached FAWNT Intersection; via the SHAAM STAR. Upon programming they noted there was no 'bottom' altitude to set; in fact no bottom altitude anywhere on the arrival or the six transitions thereof. ATC then asked if they were going to make their 9;000 restriction at GREGS for which the only charted restriction is 'At 250 KT.'

B757 flight crew reports forgetting to set the flaps to takeoff prior to taking the runway; due to a long taxi in low visibility and fatigue. Autothrust will not engage on the runway and when thrust is pushed up to taxi clear the takeoff warning sounds.

First Officer notes a number of alerts being displayed on the EAD that did not make sense during preflight. Going below it is discovered that the tether used to keep the nose wheel from lifting off the ground during loading is too long. The tether is quickly shortened by ground personnel.

While troubleshooting a flight crew report of Rudder-Aileron Trim wheel binding on a CE-560XL; an Aircraft Maintenance Inspector finds the Autopilot Control wire bundle tangled in the Rudder-Aileron Trim Assembly vertical shafts; inside the aft end of the cockpit Center pedestal. Inspector questions if a Task Card for inspecting the routing and security of wire bundles and tie-wraps had been accomplished.

Captain of a Learjet-31A aircraft reports he felt a slight 'catch' in the aileron controls during departure lift-off. Concerns for possible flight controls binding; pilot decides to do a precautionary return to field.

Pitts pilot reports a weather divert to BWG and landing without announcing on the CTAF. Pilot neglects to make announcement due fear of looking down to tune at low altitude and the poor forward visibility of his aircraft. During roll out; a business jet is observed going around overhead.
VNY Ground Controller describes a loss of separation with a faster aircraft over taking a slower aircraft on departure.
ZID Controller describes a flight break up that wasn't the usual type of break up resulting in an airspace violation.
PCT Controller and pilots of the aircraft describe an airspace violation.
show: 2014-11 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Climb

text: When their flaps refused to extend beyond five degrees on approach the flight crew of a B737 opted to go around to troubleshoot the problem.  When fuel remaining became an issue they [advised ATC] and; during the subsequent approach; the flaps this time extended normally.

B737 flight crew reports leveling at 13;000 feet crossing RIOOS on the TRALR5 with the intention of climbing to FL190 after passing TRALR; as stated in the routing box. ATC is not happy with this interpretation of the verbiage and the crew is told to continue climb to FL190.
B767 flight crew detects electrical fumes in the cockpit at FL350 and elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: B737 Captain reports the First Officer (F/O) cleared his O2 mask and noted the O2 pressure dropped to zero in flight. Seconds later the pressure returned to 950 PSI. Arrival station Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) found O2 bottle handle only one-quarter turn opened. Captain had made logbook write-up at previous station suspecting bottle was 'closed'; but was assured the O2 handle was 'open'.

An international B757 flight received their PDC clearance via CPDLC and noted it contained no 'revised segment' annotation although there was a 'LOAD' prompt on one of the CDU displayed pages and opted to leave their filed route programmed in the FMS.  After takeoff ATC cleared them to a fix that was not in their filed route at which time they learned the route had been revised and was available to them had they activated the 'LOAD' prompt.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Parked

text: B747 First Officer describes routine runway and arrival changes that are issued by ATC during arrival to ZBAA. In addition; the arrival designations printed on Jeppesen charts and used by ATC do not match the designations used by the Honeywell FMC.
B757 Captain experiences a near ground collision with a vehicle that cuts in front of the aircraft while being marshalled into the gate.
B777 Captain reports being unable to turn off the runway after landing due to the tiller being jammed on the First Officer's side by the unused iPad mount.
A B747-400 flight crew received an EICAS STAB GREENBAND warning during pushback; conducted the associated QRH procedure and returned to the gate for assistance.  A subsequent dispatch was successful.
A CRJ-700 flight crew declared an emergency; executed a controlled emergency descent; and diverted to a suitable airport when the Captain's windshield arced and then shattered at FL350.

EMB-175 Captain experiences a jet bridge collision with the aircraft while the agents are attempting to remove it after boarding. A different agent is able to get the jetbridge clear and the aircraft is carefully inspected; with no damage found. During taxi the aircraft pulls to the right and the Captain elects to return to the gate.
HS-125-800XP Captain reported wake vortex encounter in 10-mile trail of a B767 on arrival to LAS.

When inappropriate electrical anomalies resulted from the removal of ground power after engine start the Captain of a DHC-8 asked that ground power be restored.  When ramp personnel alerted the flight deck to smoke and sparks emanating from the left engine the engines were shut down; the passengers evacuated and both fire bottles were emptied into the left engine as a precaution.

McDonnell Douglas Heavy Captain experiences difficulty moving the speedbrake handle in flight and applies more pressure. The result is a roll to the left which is first detected by the First Officer and corrected. During approach the spoilers are armed and function normally on landing.
A ramp member was injured when opening a cabin door of an A310 while the cabin was pressurized due to a regulator failure.
Pilot reports of violating Class Delta airspace while under flight following.

Flight Attendant finds an elderly woman seated in the exit row; who boarded early and used a wheelchair. When queried as to her ability to assist in an emergency she responds in the affirmative and is allowed to stay in her seat. A Supervisor contacted after the flight indicates that if exit row passengers are queried and respond in the affirmative that is all that is required by the FAR.

A Maintenance Technician narrowly avoided serious injury while darting in front of a running engine to retrieve tools during a maintenance procedure. Loose items from his pockets were ingested by the engine.
Pilot reports of being under flight following and violating another Tower's airspace.
Pilot reports of possibly violating LAX Class Bravo.
SRQ Tower Controller reports of a runway incursion due to a missed readback.
CCR Tower Controller reports of a reported NMAC by an aircraft that did not report a 2 mile left base.
ZTL Controller reports while trying to separate two aircraft another Center violates airspace which distracts the ZTL Controller.
EWR Tower Controller describes a go-around that then becomes a conflict with an aircraft inbound to another close proximity airport..

ZLA Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is auto handedoff to him but is already in his airspace.  He doesn't observe the target and coordinates with another sector who is handing off the aircraft to him.
MEM Tower Local Control describes a situation where they had to take an aircraft out for resequence due to its speed on final.
When the flight crew of a B737NG reprogrammed their FMS to comply with a takeoff runway change they failed to note that an enroute fix was not included.  ATC advised and they corrected.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: Pilot reports of speed changes assigned by ATC not in compliance with what is on the arrival.  Also the pilot describes in the scenario late runway changes.

B737 Captain laments the lack of a Cuban overflight permit number while avoiding thunderstorms adjacent to Cuban airspace. He also believes that iPad displayed enroute charts cannot take the place of paper charts due to the lack notes and the difficulty bring what notes are available using the touchscreen in turbulence.
The flight crew of an EMB-145 declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport after smelling a foul odor also detected in the cabin by passengers.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: MD-83 flight crew experiences a landing gear indication failure during approach; with two green indications and the right main with no indication. The light test switch indicated the bulbs were burned out and a go-around is initiated to troubleshoot. Bulb assemblies are swapped to the inoperative position but due not indicate green and will not test. Upon returning the bulb assemblies to their original positions they no longer function. After a flyby a normal landing ensues.
An MD-11 flight crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport upon receipt of Level three CRG Fire Aft warnings.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A transoceanic B777 flight crew; after leveling at cruise altitude; was advised by the purser of smoke/fumes and a smoke detector alarm sounding in the upper crew rest area and passenger reports of light grey haze/smoke in the cabin.  Prompt decisions were made to divert to an airport ahead of them and to dump fuel while doing so to expedite a landing.  Problems with ATC and flight deck communications while wearing 02 masks; access to approach plates for their diversion airport--including a frustrating failure by both first officers to obtain them via their tablet EFB--and finding appropriate checklists increased flight crew workload to significant levels.  Approach chart/airport information was ultimately obtained from ATC and via the navigation database.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A B757 Captain reported sighting a large model airplane or helicopter about 100 FT below and 500 FT laterally away from them as they were on base leg for Runway 22L at JFK.
Pilot reports of a go-around due to not being able to see if the departing heavy aircraft was actually airborne.
show: 2014-11 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: B767 flight crew experiences a right wing slide caution message during initial climb on a ferry flight after an A check by Maintenance. The QRH is consulted and the right wing is examined visually with no deployment noted. During approach; as the flaps are extended from 20 to 30; a noise is heard and vibration is felt. The Tower reports something trailing from the aircraft and possible smoke coming from the lower rear fuselage. A normal landing ensues.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Landing
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: B737-800 Captain reported encountering jet blast and resulting turbulence from an aircraft taking off shortly before landing at SNA. Reporter stated this tight spacing is common practice in SNA and he is not comfortable with it.
A B777-300 flight crew; nearing the end of a 14 hour flight; discussed the difficulties and distractions of reprogramming and complying with ATC alterations to RNAV STAR 'descend via' clearances.
Pilot reports of landing at a military airport and seeing arresting gear on the runway.

While deadheading in the cabin and sitting in the last row of an EMB-145 aircraft; a Captain notices a section of the left wing trailing edge skin cavitating; collapsing at cruise altitude. Skin distortion appeared to go back to normal below 10;000 feet and remained smooth with flaps extended for landing.
Flight crew opted to divert to the nearest suitable airport after the First Officer's side window shattered with a loud bang at FL360.
A319 flight crew reported the aircraft moved about nine feet after setting the brakes at the gate. Crew reported brake pressure was in the green when the brakes were set.
Pilot reports of an NMAC caused by the Tower Controller sequencing traffic and not issuing traffic.

When cleared by Clearance Delivery to 'climb via' the PHX SNOBL RNAV departure off the east runway complex the flight crew of a Falcon 50 climbed so as to cross GOALY at or below 9;000 FT as depicted on the graphic and described in the INITIAL CLIMB text box. As they climbed through 8;000 FT ATC advised they were required to maintain 8;000 FT as stated in the ROUTING text box.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Climb

text: A320 First Officer reported encountering wake vortex in 6 miles trail of a B757 on approach to LAX that rolled the aircraft up to 60 degrees. Reporter cited wind conditions as probably contributory.
show: 2014-09 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: Following the loss of both packs due to right and left engine bleed air failures the flight crew of a B757 diverted to a nearby airport and landed safely.
The instructor and IFR training pilots aboard a PA28R suffered a partial power loss; advised ATC; and landed at the airport where they had been shooting practice ILS approaches.
B757 First Officer reported losing cabin pressure when both pneumatic bleeds failed at FL350.

A student pilot with his flight instructor overheard their position announced to an aircraft transitioning the airport area; but they were not provided position information in regard to the traffic. They were surprised to find themselves in a near-mid-air-collision situation and took evasive action.

A C525B flight crew on a vector to intercept the localizer suffered an NMAC with an unidentified aircraft.  Their decision to stop the turn to intercept; causing them to fly through the localizer; may have been a contributing factor.
Pilot reports of being questioned about violating Class C airspace; while being under flight following from the overlying TRACON.
Pilot reports of advising ATC while under flight following that he was descending to avoid clouds.  While doing so he entered a Class D airspace.
Three pilots report extremely dangerous behavior by the pilot of a biplane operating in the traffic pattern of a non-towered airport.

BE-95 pilot experiences a gear failure during landing resulting in damage to the aircraft and a runway excursion. Upon being lifted the main gear are found to be partially extended and the nose gear is retracted.
BJC Controller reports of another controller prompting a pilot to cancel IFR to remain in the pattern at the airport.
show: 2014-11 · ATC Issue All Types · Final Approach

text: B737-300 flight crew experiences an autopilot disconnect horn after the TO/GA button is pushed during takeoff. The takeoff is rejected and troubleshooting indicates that the autopilot must have been engaged at some time during preflight and not detected until the TO/GA button was pushed. A child visitor to the cockpit may have pushed the button during preflight.
Flight crew experiences a stuck mic during initial climb and attribute the problem to the combination of a new ACP and a Bose headset. When the headset is unplugged the stuck mic goes away.

B737 Captain reports not writing up a Standby Power Check failure due to being admonished by the Chief Pilot on a previous occasion. The Standby power Check is no longer a flight crew function and is checked only by Maintenance.

After landing with nearly full fuel tanks in just above freezing conditions the flight crew of a B737NG planned--but failed--to check the tops of the wings for cold soaked fuel frost prior to their subsequent takeoff.  A lengthy layover permitting intervening distractions may have been a contributing factor.
B737-700 Captain experiences an EGPWS terrain caution at 6;600 feet during a night visual approach to Runway 16R at RNO and goes around.

B757 flight crew experiences a Right Bleed EICAS Message followed by a Left Bleed EICAS message; resulting in loss of both PACKS which results in a CABIN ALT warning. Flight diverts to a suitable airport.

A B737 First Officer addressed the decades old problem of misinterpreted PDC clearances and subsequent deviations due to their ambiguous and confusing formatting.  He further provided a simple; on point suggestion he believes would eliminate the majority of such errors and make air travel safer.
B737-800 flight crew reported erroneous EGPWS terrain warning over the threshold of FLL Runway 28L.
B757-200 Captain reported engine failure after takeoff. Flight returned to departure airport.
CRJ-200 Captain describes a missed approach which results from poor ATC handling during vectors for an ILS approach at SFO.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: CRJ-200 flight crew describes a night IMC ILS to minimums with the First Officer flying. The mic is keyed multiple times by both pilots on the CTAF to bring up the runway lights. At minimums the runway is in sight but the lights appear to be off and the mic is keyed again with negative results. A normal landing ensues and the lights come on bright during taxi in. The Captain was new to the seat and on high minimums; and the First Officer was new to the airline.

B777 First Officer describes difficulties with clearances on a flight from the USA to Europe. Initial clearance no PDC; obtained via voice. Oceanic clearance obtained via voice with many additional questions. CPDLC is sporadic and HF position reports are required. Shannon Control asks many additional questions and issues a major reroute without explanation. The Dispatcher indicates they are using a form of shorthand to file flight plans; which may be causing the difficulty.
During pushback; a Ramp Worker chooses to open the cargo door and deposit late bags without communicating with the flight crew.
A ramp employee is concerned about the need for agents to walk across an active runway after pushback.

Inefficient ATC handling resulting in part from communications problems due to language barriers resulted in an unstabilized approach for an A330 which nonetheless resulted in an on-speed touchdown in the first thousand feet of the runway.

An A321 flight crew landing in VMC on Runway 28L at FLL received a GPWS Terrain warning as they crossed the threshold; closing the throttles for landing.  The reporter suspects the 55 foot raised elevation at the approach end of the runway and the 'seawall' type structure supporting it contributed to a false warning.
CE-560XL Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to JFK in trail of a B757.
show: 2014-11 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: CE750 pilot experiences an intense acrid smell descending out of FL390 and the cockpit pack is turned off. The odor persists and the cabin pack is turned off and the cockpit pack turned on. Oxygen masks are donned; an emergency declared and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Descent
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: On initial climbout; B757 flight crew observed EICAS messages for L PACK OFF & L ENG BLEED OFF. The switches are turned off per the QRH and shortly after the R PACK & R BLEED began cycling on & off and also the R CTR FUEL TANK PUMP. The crew elects to return to the departure airport.

When the flight crew of an MD-80; descending via the BRDJE RNAV STAR to DFW; began their descent from 11;000 feet to 8;000 feet as ROCKZ became their active waypoint approach control advised they had failed to cross the previous waypoint; STONZ; at the required 11;000 feet; a deviation ATC said was becoming common. The reporters believe this may happen due to the 45 degree left course change at STONZ--performed by the Lateral Nav Function of their FMS--the fact that STONZ is a 'fly by' waypoint and their aircraft's lack of automated VNAV thus requiring manual execution of the required descent; an execution for which they utilize the switch from the previous active waypoint to the next.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: B757 flight crew experiences an L and R Bleed EICAS message during climb. Examining the overhead panel reveals that the packs are off and the bleeds are off and the APU is running; indicating the after start checklist was never accomplished. The switches are set right and the flight continues to destination.

An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes the progressive troubleshooting that he and another Technician applied to locate the cause of a whirling sound coming from the Right-Hand (R/H) Leading Edge Anti-Ice ducts on a Cessna CE-560XLS aircraft. Damage also found to Heat Blankets used to protect the fuel tanks from excessive duct heat was caused by missing; undersized and deteriorated orange colored O-Rings at pneumatic duct connections.

Pilot describes a situation where he is under flight following and then vectored at an altitude to enter the Class Bravo airspace; but terminated just before entering it.  The pilot had to enter the airspace and then request a clearance to be in it.

The First Officer of a Gulfstream G200 related repeated attempts to get the Captain's attention to their divergent track and altitude while attempting to fly the ILS Runway 6 to TEB during turbulent but VMC. Following a low altitude alert from the Tower they began a go-around but then picked up the airport and landed safely. The reporter attributed the Captain's disorientation to automation dependency.
show: 2014-11 · Flight Deck: Other / Unknown · Final Approach

text: The pilot of a C172 experienced a runway excursion after landing and contacted a taxiway sign.
Due to time pressure and a communication error; an experienced flight instructor entered the active runway and took off while a soloing student pilot was on final approach.
LVK Controller reports of an aircraft on final without its gear down.  Local Control Developmental advises the pilot the gear isn't down and pilot cycles gear; lands safely.
show: 2014-11 · ATC Issue All Types · Final Approach

text: The flight crew of a B737NG was switched to and landed on Runway 28L at FLL after failing to recall a company restriction to not do so.  They received a nuisance GPWS alert just at touchdown.
B737-300 First Officer reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning on a night visual approach to DAL Runway 31R. A go-around was performed in response to the alert.
Air Carrier First Officer reports being zapped by a green laser over London during approach. He describes the physical effects and recovery process over the next five days.

A319 Captain reports being cleared for takeoff on 1R at LAS; with the additional requirement to keep the preceding A320 in sight. The takeoff is delayed until the A320 rotates and results in a formation takeoff with a Hawker on 1L. The reporter believes the Tower is not providing proper separation.

G450 Flight Crew reports setting an incorrect altimeter setting (30.58 vs 29.58) during descent and approach. This error is not discovered until ATC issues a low altitude alert at the same time the crew receives a GPWS warning. Fatigue was cited as a factor by both pilots.
B737 pilots report of being cleared for takeoff then Tower clearing another aircraft to cross downfield.  Pilots abort takeoff.
A300-600 flight crew reported brake over temp after takeoff. They declared an emergency and diverted to nearest suitable airport.

First Officer reports being instructed by IND Ground to hold in the Juliet pad short of Papa while troubleshooting a pneumatic problem. An A300 is noticed taxiing west on Papa and it appears a conflict will develop. The flight crew flashes their lights and a last second jink to the left by the A300 avoids the collision.

The flight crew of an A300 taxiing on Papa for takeoff on Runway 23R at IND moved slightly left of centerline while they passed a Heavy Mcdonnell Douglas aircraft holding in the pad at the intersection with Juliet; believing the surface markings provided adequate clearance. The next day the flight crew of the Mcdonnell Douglas advised the A300's wingtip had come within five feet of their windshield even given their precautionary deviation.

Premier 1 flight crew reports diverting for a longer runway after a FLAPS FAIL indication. A flaps up landing with the First Officer flying is planned but the vector is close to the FAF and the autopilot overshoots causing ATC to issue a go around. The second approach is successful.
The pilot of a turbine powered experimental aircraft experienced a flame out and emergency landing due to air in the fuel control system.

ZAU Controller describes a situation while working a D side position and the R side controller not following the SOP and ending up with numerous separation errors.  The Controller did not issue Descend Via clearances.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: C90 FLM describes a situation where an aircraft is issued direct a fix but the aircraft turns towards another fix that is similar sounding but in a different state.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: CRQ Controllers report of an aircraft that gets a flat tire while exiting the runway but stops within the safety area of the runway.  Operations continue even though the aircraft is in the safety area.
ZHU Developmental describes a situation where he had to deny practice approaches to numerous aircraft due to workload.

B777 Flight Crew reports encountering severe clear air turbulence in RJJJ airspace; causing an overspeed warning initially then a 1000 foot altitude loss. The crew is able to return to the assigned altitude then to FL350 for a smooth ride. No injuries are reported.

During FMC programing an Air Carrier Captain discovers that the filed SID does not exist in the FMC; nor in his chart manual. The company is contacted and it is learned that the new procedures are effective this day but were not available in base the day prior.

Pilot describes a situation where they are in a descent and get a RA at the same time the Controller issues traffic.  They descend as the RA suggests and turn to a heading issued by the Controller.  Traffic is not seen but suggested to be a drone by the pilot.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: CRJ-200 Captain reported directional control difficulties on takeoff roll on ORD Runway 22L when they encountered jet blast from a B777 on takeoff from Runway 28R.
show: 2014-11 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: A flight instructor was attempting to demonstrate a short field landing to the pilot owner when he neglected to lower the landing gear; resulting in a gear-up landing.

A Boeing C17 flight crew inadvertently responded and complied with clearances intended for another aircraft with a similar call sign.  The flight was not advised at the time and the reporter only learned of the incident approximately a month after it occurred.
show: 2014-10 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: BE36 pilot reports landing at an uncontrolled airport with the AWOS reporting marginal VFR and 3 SM visibility. He believes the visibility was greater than 4 SM but was contacted by an FAA Safety Inspector regarding the legality of the landing.
Pilot reports of numerous runway and approach changes inbound to destination airport.
A B737 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when the right rudder pedal was heavy and input unresponsive.

B737 Captain arriving MMMX notes that taxiway B6 is NOTAMed closed; but does not expect it to be a factor. After arrival and runway changes; and numerous speed adjustment by ATC; the NOTAM is forgotten about until it does become a factor.
An air carrier ramp worker is concerned about jet bridge misalignment due to aircraft not being able to track the gate centerline due to a dogleg lead-in line.
CRJ200 Flight Crew reports confusing a GLD UNSAFE caution message and a GLD NOT ARMED message and ended up preforming the wrong procedure for landing.
EMB-145LR Captain reported deviating from cleared track on departure when the flying First Officer called for LNAV prematurely.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Takeoff

text: B777 International First Officer and Relief Pilot report getting a stick shaker on climbout from EGLL when the autothrottle pulled the thrust levers back following a minor crew error in FMS setup.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Climb

text: Beechcraft King Air 200 pilot reported losing the No. 1 right bus; followed a few minutes later by the No. 1 left bus; which resulted in loss of EFIS and cockpit lights.

Twice in the same day the flight crew of an EMB-145 found themselves flummoxed by the demands of the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD with the flight crew; the FMC and ATC unable to resolve the complexities of altitudes restrictions and traffic separation.
CRJ-700 flight crew reported they received a brake overheat warning on climbout. After troubleshooting the decision was made to continue to destination.

CRJ-200 flight crew experienced a rudder trim issue causing the aircraft to yaw to the left during the descent phase.  The crew landed at their destination airport. During taxi the crew followed the wrong yellow line and ended up on the de-ice pad.
B767-300F flight crew reported LE and TE flaps and slats would not extend on approach. An emergency was declared and a zero flap approach and landing safely flown.
CRJ-200 First Officer reported encountering wake vortex in 6-mile trail of a B757 on approach to SLC.
show: 2014-11 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: A320 flight crew reports being dispatched with the number four spoiler set deactivated by Maintenance to comply with an MEL procedure. With two symmetrical X's appearing over two spoilers on the flight control page the crew assumes the procedure has been done correctly. In cruise another ECAM spoiler fault is annunciated and two additional X's are noted on the flight control page. It is determined that Maintenance deactivated the wrong spoiler pair. Spoilers are not numbered on the flight control page.

First Officer reported there was a procedural deviation during preflight deice procedures that was not discovered until they had taxied to the runway. The flight took off even though the reporter realized later they should have returned to the gate for proper deice procedure.
A320 First Officer reported descending early on the VOR-DME-2 Runway 16 approach to MMSD; citing chart confusion and poor ATC communications as contributing.
show: 2014-11 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: A small transport jet flight crew reported they ran over a coyote on landing roll in TWF; no apparent damage to the aircraft.
ATR-42 flight crew reported losing cabin pressure in descent. They were able to control pressurization with manual control but landed with pressure exceeding the limit.
Air carrier Dispatcher reported concerns that overly complex MEL procedures and documentation could lead to errors.
show: 2014-11 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: Large Transport Captain reported possible issue with the aircraft pitot/static system or the FMS data load that generates a speed too slow for configuration.
The wingtip of a C172 came in contact with the propeller of an operating Small Aircraft twin engine when the pilot of the Cessna strayed off the taxiway centerline.

The pilot of a Cessna 150 experienced an engine stopped on climbout and was able to land on the remaining runway.  He reported likely fuel contamination that was not detectable during normal fuel sump draining.
A Mooney pilot reported a gear collapse on landing. The Mechanic that had previously repaired the landing gear system provided more details on the event.
A pilot performing a pipeline inspection contacted an unknown object in-flight and observed an airframe vibration.  He elected to land at the nearby airport to access the damage.
Pilot reports of possibly violating restricted airspace after being told that it was inactive; by ATC.

A CL30 flight crew cleared to depart DAL on the JPOOL SID off Runway 31R was surprised when the autopilot attempted to turn left direct to TTT vice fly the charted 'headings for vectors' northeast of TTT.
show: 2014-11 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: BUR Tower controllers report of a go-around that cannot be kept in the traffic pattern at the airport and is handed off to approach for sequencing.
show: 2014-11 · Airspace Violation All Types · Final Approach

text: ZID Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is outside of a Restricted Area maneuvering while IFR.
ZUA Controller describes a flight split up where the second aircraft is already separated from the flight lead.

ZAB Controller describes climbing an aircraft to its requested altitude; then after 10 minutes the pilot advises the CPC that they need to descend.  CPC tells pilot in a few minutes for opposite direction traffic; pilot descends anyway causing a loss of separation.
