text: Air carrier crew responded to insufficient thrust warning during takeoff roll and rejected the takeoff.

A crew pushed back from the EWR C Concourse with clearance to disconnect at a gate near Taxiway RG; then taxi via B; D; Hold Short of V. Because of signage confusion the crew taxied out the throat to A then S; D to hold at V.
CRJ-700 pilot reported they were advised they failed to meet crossing restrictions on the HABBS3 STAR arrival into CYUL.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: Air carrier Captain reported an NMAC with a helicopter shortly after takeoff from MAF airport.

Air carrier Captain reported EWR Terminal A taxi lines between Taxiways RA and RC are faded; hard to follow; and may allow aircraft to taxi closer to the terminal and into unsafe proximity to parked aircraft.

All three B777 pilots failed to notice Flap 20 set for landing even though the First Officer; flying pilot; call Flaps 25. The Captain missed the earlier Flaps 25 call but a 1;000 feet stabilized approach call is no longer required.
A321 flight crew reported executing a go-around after experiencing uncommanded thrust on approach to LAX.
MD-83 Captain reported he was not properly notified of a shipment of Li-metal batteries on his flight.

CRJ200 flight crew reported a rejected takeoff after deicing due to the flaps not being set for takeoff. ATC miscues helped precipitate the chain of events that led up to this RTO; but the current requirement to keep the flaps up after deicing until takeoff clearance is received was the final straw.

A CRJ-700 EICAS alerted R BLEED DUCT at cruise altitude. The crew completed the immediate action checklist which closed both bleed valves and depressurized the cabin. The cabin oxygen masks deployed during descent to 10;000 feet and diversion to a nearby airport.
Aircrew experienced an in-flight engine failure and successfully diverted to an interim airport.
Student pilot under instruction flared too high resulting in a stall. Aircraft struck the runway with enough force to cause damage; but no crew injuries resulted.

While flying a VOR approach in VMC conditions; GA pilot misinterpreted the GPS approach presentation and descended early. This resulted in flight below minimum altitude for that location and subsequent ATC altitude alert call. By the time the radio call for the altitude alert was completed; the aircraft was inside the FAF and at a safe altitude.

G-IV Captain was informed by ATC that he had leveled off at 2100 feet on the RUUDY5 while all three aircraft altimeters show 1500 feet. A few minutes later the aircraft altimeters agree with the Mode C read out. Thirty minutes into the flight the number two air data computer failed. The aircraft had been deiced just prior to departure.

The TRACON Controller observed an unidentified VFR aircraft depart an airport on a converging course with an air carrier on a visual approach to an adjacent airport already in communication with the Tower. The TRACON Controller pointed the traffic out to the Tower Local Controller. The air carrier responded to a TCAS RA.

An aircraft was making an emergency descent. ATC issued a heading to opposite direction climbing traffic to avoid the descending traffic. The climbing traffic turned to the wrong heading causing a conflict with the emergency descending traffic.
An aircraft in a refueling track departed the refueling track and began its flight back to its base without a clearance.
B737 Captain reported tugs that are outfitted with LED headlights blind the flight crew resulting in difficulty seeing the safety zone and/or the Marshaller.

B737-700 Captain experienced an over speed during descent in VNAV with the speed programed to .78/284 for no apparent reason. Speed increased from .78 to .82 Mach; without turning on the engine anti ice or a wind shift.

On approach in a B737; ATC issued an improper vector which sent the flight crew through the localizer. While attempting to recapture the localizer and glideslope the flight crew began to fall behind the aircraft resulting in breaking out of the clouds to the right of the runway.

B767 flight crew experienced an unusual vibration and excessive noise coming from the nosewheel area after gear retraction. They returned to departure airport where Maintenance determined that the connecting rod from nose landing gear to the nose gear door was disconnected.

An A320 pilot reported that when the destination airport ILS was selected; the frequency defaulted to a previously 'Hard' tuned frequency. Once the Flight Crew cleared the 'Hard' frequency they got the proper signal for the ILS. Later it was uncovered that Maintenance had manually entered a unused frequency in the ILS for an Autoland test and had not cleared it. This frequency turned out to be the ILS for an airport nearby the destination airport.
Shut down #1 engine due to loss of oil pressure.
Flight crew lost control of the aircraft when they encountered black ice on the taxiway. They regained control and continued with extreme caution.
show: 2016-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: B737-900 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence departing JFK in trail of a B757.
show: 2016-01 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Climb

text: Flight crew neglected to connect the generators due to not completing the checklist properly. Transitioning from old procedures to new procedures caused the flight crew to get out of sequence while accomplishing the checklist.

Air carrier flight crew reported the iPad's navigational software did an update automatically causing it to go to a black screen then to the home screen. This causes the iPad as a navigation aid to be undependable.

Air carrier Captain reported being cleared for a visual approach to Runway 4 at ELP and commencing descent only to discover that terrain was between the aircraft and the runway. The terrain was cleared and the approach was continued.

The Captain thought that the weather was improving and that it would be at or above minimums at the ETA and therefore it was legal to depart; while the Dispatcher did not. The Dispatcher held the flight until the weather improved to minimums.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: After troubleshooting and replacing the #1 Stabilizer Control Unit on a CRJ-701 Maintenance was told to replace the Linear Actuator for the Pitch/Trim system. Before installing the replacement actuator it had to be sequenced and rigged using a variable power supply. Since they didn't have one available; Maintenance Control told the maintenance crew to use the battery on the aircraft as a power supply. Maintenance refused until the proper power supply was available.
During a postflight walkaround; Aircraft Maintenance Technician discovered the #1 engine pylon access panel was missing.
A320 First Officer reports discovering Enroute that NRS waypoint KD45U has been inadvertently entered into the FMC as KD54U. This is detected and corrected before a significant deviation results.
show: 2015-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: Cruising in a PA28-235 at 9;000 feet the ATC instruction was to climb to 11;000 feet where the aircraft began to accumulate ice. Requested a lower altitude but ATC denied the request due to altitude restrictions in that area. Temporarily lost communication with ATC and landed at the nearest airport. After landing; the leading edges of the wings and stabilator were still significantly iced over.
During takeoff in a Piper PA-12 the engine failed and the pilot notified the tower; returned; and landed without incident.
After a quick decent from 11;500 ft. in a Navion Rangemaster; the engine failed to power up. The engine restarted successfully after performing a Fuel; Mixture; Switches check.
show: 2015-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Final Approach

text: A PA-28 pilot reported encountering ice during an IFR flight cannot avoid icing at 3;600 feet required by ATC. He is prompted to declare an emergency or cancel IFR and chooses the later. The approach was successful.
PA28 pilot on short final to Runway 30 at WHP experienced a NMAC with a drone flying in the opposite direction.

Twin engine aircraft with an engine out emergency attempted to land conducting an ILS approach. The aircraft was unable to intercept the localizer twice. ATC vectored the aircraft on to an ASR approach and the aircraft landed.
A90 TRACON Controller had difficulty coordinating a point out with a Tower. After approving the point out; the Tower departed an aircraft into a confliction with the pointed out aircraft.

A flight plan for an active enroute flight was removed from the ATC system. The aircraft's 'full' data block dropped off the Controller's scope and only a partial data block remained on the radar display. The controllers did not notice for approximately 50 miles and did not realize an aircraft was flying through their airspace.
Aircraft had a ground near miss with another aircraft while taking the runway for departure.
Aircraft on a non-precision approach executed a go around due to heavy rain at the missed approach point. The flight crew then decided to divert to a more suitable airport.
B737-700 flight crew configured flaps to briefed position late in the approach just before touchdown.
First Officer comments that on his new fleet all Captains use the overhead speaker for all ATC communications.
During test flight left engine EICAS indicated overheats. Engine secured and flight landed single engine.

A flight crew reported encountering windshear conditions on final approach and performed a go-around. The missed approach maneuver was successfully accomplished; however dynamic flight conditions resulted in a deviation from their assigned altitude.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Final Approach

text: A ramp agent's hand was caught beneath a belt loader's moving belt which nearly pulled him out of a B757's rear cargo. Both belt emergency stop activation buttons had been removed.

A321 flight crew reported observing a #2 engine N1 overspeed warning during the takeoff roll. The Captain aborted the takeoff and returned to the gate for maintenance. This event was originally thought to be a low speed abort; however the takeoff was actually rejected at 90 knots.
DHC-8-200 Captain reported returning to the departure airport after shutting down a malfunctioning engine.
A C208 pilot described his physiological 'buzzed' feeling after exposure to TKS anti-ice fluid in flight during freezing IMC conditions.

While enroute; a CRJ-900 crew thought fuel was decreasing more rapidly than expected and assumed a fuel leak. After landing a fuel odor was detected; but no leak discovered so the aircraft was ferried to a maintenance station.

Airbus Captain experienced a loss of V speeds during the takeoff roll resulting in the First Officer calling V1 well before the actual V1 and the Captain initiating rotation. The Captain notes the sluggish rotation and the aircraft is allowed to fly off the runway.

A320 flight crew reported encountering a bird strike at high speed during the takeoff roll. The takeoff was continued; however a significant vibration in one engine was noted. They reduced power on the affected engine and safely returned to the departure airport; where major damage to the engine was discovered.
CRJ-900 flight crew reported a heading deviation occurred when the pilot not flying misunderstood the pilot flying's request.
EMB170 First Officer reported being level at 17;000 feet then assigned FL180 by ATC. The altimeter is not reset to 29.92 until reaching 18000 feet resulting is a 200 foot overshoot.
EMB-145 flight crew reported overshooting a crossing altitude when a late runway change caused confusion and distraction.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: CRJ-200 flight crew reported they began takeoff roll with flaps incorrectly set; but caught it early in the roll and rejected the takeoff.
A321 Captain reported his takeoff clearance was cancelled by ATC because of conflicting traffic.
A319 First Officer reported a flap overspeed on arrival; citing overreliance on automation as a contributing factor.
B737 flight crew reported executing an autoland even though the Captain's Master light was not illuminated as required.

B737 Captain reported that new First Officers the he flies with are under the mistaken impression that they must brief the engine inoperative go-around procedure for every approach to an airport with a special engine out missed approach procedure.

CRJ-900 flight crew reported taking off with flaps set to 8 when they should have been set to 20; after several runway changes by ATC during taxi out. The Captain described the First Officer as being well behind the aircraft.

B737-800 flight crew reported being cleared for takeoff behind a B757 without wake turbulence separation. The Tower is queried and states that the separation standards have been changed. The Flight Manual for the company involved does not reflect those changes.

A PA31 flight crew reported a loss of control during landing with the First Officer flying. The landing had been normal up until the brakes were applied; then the aircraft began a slow turn to the left rapidly increasing to a full skidding rotation to the left with a runway excursion.

Flight Attendant reported sitting between flights in an inhospitable company conference room in the middle of the night as part of a regular; fatiguing crew sequence with inadequate rest accommodations.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: CRJ-200 Flight Attendant reported that the seat backs in rows 12 and 13 were not secured in the upright position. There are no procedures; information; or education regarding these seat backs and how they are supposedly meant to allow access to emergency equipment.
A B737 Flight Attendant described a continuous duty over night during which only one hour of actual sleep is obtained.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: A pilot was cleared to cross the runway and hesitantly began crossing but detected an approaching aircraft and stopped just over the hold short line. The approaching aircraft executed a go-around.
A student pilot reported making multiple left hand closed pattern approaches but was then told to make right traffic. After he failed to turn right downwind ATC notified the Pilot of a near miss.
A PA23 pilot receiving instruction reported a right gear collapse after a firm landing with a slight bounce. The aircraft became uncontrollable and went off the right side of the runway.

A sight seeing Helicopter Pilot reported a near miss with another touring helicopter after converging over Black Point near Hoover Dam. One helicopter pilot was in the right seat while the other pilot flew left seat and neither pilot saw the other.

An ACA Scout pilot reported a runway excursion after landing due to a gust of wind. Power is applied and the aircraft is flown back to base. Post flight revealed damage to the right wingtip and the aircraft is subsequently flown to another airport for repairs.

A PA-31T corporate pilot reported his aircraft made a 180 degree turn while IMC after a faulty alternator output affected the Captain's HSI; Flight Director and autopilot. GPS heading was flown to the VMC alternate airport.

A Cessna pilot reported an apparent loss of engine power while climbing out of the traffic pattern. After advising ATC and performing a successful return to the field; the pilot discovered that the fuel shutoff valve had been closed rather than the cabin heat valve opened as intended.
ZSE Controller issued an IFR clearance altitude below the Minimum Enroute Altitude for the airway.

HCF Controller reported of saving an operational error due to correcting the aircraft altitude. Controller released aircraft off on a 320 heading. Aircraft came off on a 020 heading and was a conflict for an arrival. Controller stopped the departing aircraft altitude and then corrected the heading.

B737 Captain described over speeds during VNAV arrivals and departures caused by FMC software and believes that updating the software would be less expensive than over speed inspections and smoother for the passengers.

B737-800 flight crew experienced aircraft damage during gate arrival when the left scimitar winglet contacted a catering truck. The truck was parked outside the safety zone but very close to it and the aircraft; under a Marshalls direction; was on the lead in line.

At about 1;000 feet after departure; a B737-700 encountered a bird flock which caused left engine surging. The aircraft returned to the departure airport where severe left engine damage was discovered as well as bird remains in the functioning right engine.
B737 flight crew experienced a GPWS terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 33 at BUR and went around. The second visual approach was successful.
A Captain taxiing at night to LAX Runway 24L via Taxiway D-8; E-8 became confused because the signage and lighting were reportedly not clear.

When the B737-800 engine and APU bleeds were opened after de-icing; the cockpit filled with a thick white mist so the aircraft was towed back to the gate and deplaned. The pilots became ill and were treated according to the MSDS guidelines then departed after recovering from de-ice fluid ingestion.
show: 2016-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Taxi

text: Brake system fault light illuminated at initial take-off roll. Aircrew rejected the take-off at low speed.
EMB-170 Captain discovered after arrival that six boxes had been transported; five of which contained dry ice; without being included on the cargo manifest.

CRJ-900 Captain reports being dispatched with a L BLEED inop MEL and discovers during climb that cabin pressure cannot be maintained with wing and engine anti ice on. The Captain elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.

A pilot reported that while taxiing to the gate he was notified by a Flight Attendant of a fire in the cabin. The aircraft was stopped on the taxiway and the source of the fire was identified as an E-cigarette device. The fire was quickly extinguished and the aircraft proceeded to the gate where the passengers disembarked in an orderly manner.
show: 2016-01 · Flight Deck: Passenger Electronic Device · Taxi

text: An air carrier flight crew was advised by a Flight Attendant of smoke in the cabin associated with a passenger's personal computer. The computer was removed to a safe area and an uneventful landing was accomplished at the destination airport.
show: 2016-01 · Flight Deck: Passenger Electronic Device · Cruise

text: A Dispatcher reported his Load Planner allowed an aircraft on an oceanic flight to leave the gate over gross even after discussions about removing payload because the Captain requested additional fuel because of winds.
An air freight carrier Dispatcher reported about exceeding structural limits when over fuelling an Airbus aircraft; some dispatchers continue the unsafe tankering practice.
CRJ-200 First Officer reported the APU had an uncommanded shutdown and he didn't know whether he was required to write it up or have Maintenance make the write-up.

Flight attendants are now required by the Company to carry iPads to perform preflight and safety duties. The Flight Attendant reported that there is no place to store them near the jump seats or on their person.

B737 Flight Attendant reported being held up at security with two other Flight attendants; due to paper work which the company should have provided. While waiting for the reporter and the two others; the Captain elects to board the aircraft with one Flight Attendant. Upon arrival at the aircraft the reporter explained that the full crew is required for boarding and the aircraft needed to be deplaned and a security sweep accomplished. The Captain refuses to do so.

While performing a retest; mechanics pulled three different circuit breakers which affected the nose wheel steering and the brakes which caused the loss of control and caused the aircraft to run off the taxiway into the mud.
B757 Captain reported experiencing an uncommanded 45 degree bank angle at FL370 that the reporter felt was related to jet stream activity.
An aircrew experienced a CSD (Constant Speed Drive) failure and mistakenly used the wrong checklist to remedy the situation.

LR45 Captain experienced a failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff along with a nose wheel steering fail message and elects to divert to a more suitable airport. After landing it is discovered that the nose gear strut has collapsed.
A flight instructor reported that he became distracted by his student's question during taxi and crossed onto an active runway as an air carrier began a takeoff roll.
A general aviation pilot reported a near-mid-air-collision with an aircraft at a non-towered airport that was not using a radio and was flying a non-standard pattern.

SCT Controller reported that there was confusion whether an aircraft that went on a missed approach was on an IFR code. Controller did not know if the crew were IFR or VFR and asked. Pilot stated VFR on the missed. More confusion ensued when the pilot then said they wanted to cancel IFR and go VFR to another airport.

text: Flight crew delayed climb to higher altitude due to traffic.
B737 Captain is confused by the MAYSA3 RNAV SID departing PHX; in that there is a top altitude of 8;000 feet; but in the initial climb instructions it says to cross GOALY at or below 9;000 feet.

text: Miscommunication with flight crew and tug person resulted in damage to the tow bar and aircraft.
Aircrew agreed to let a deadheading company qualified in-type pilot join the crew as a working crewmember for the trip.
Aircraft engine after pushback would not start after several attempts. Aircrew elected to return to the gate and call Maintenance. Troubled engine caught fire while Maintenance was troubleshooting.

text: Air carrier First Officer reported experiencing a GPWS warning while on a visual approach to LAS.
B737 Captain elected to return to the departure airport after the First Officer indicates the aircraft cannot be trimmed. A large fuel imbalance is noted; but suspected to be in error.
FDC NOTAM was not noticed by aircrew for a change in published altitude on arrival SFO. This is a common repeat item.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: A Boeing 737 pilot reported being hit in the eyes by a laser while on final approach at a foreign airport. The preceding aircraft also reported a laser directed at them. The pilot was not injured; and the incident was reported to airport authorities.
Dispatch is not being informed of changes in fuel loads.

The Dispatcher sent a release that was for 38;000 pounds more than actual for the aircraft; as the ballast fuel was added twice. Once by the ramp with the Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) info and again by the Dispatcher who saw the ballast fuel request; but didn't realize that the ramp had already included the ballast fuel in the ZFW.
Flight Attendant reported that the Operations Agent insisted on closing the aircraft's main cabin door while passengers were still standing. Ground Ops Supervisor was called to rectify the situation.
A flight instructor reported comments by ATC after he had activated the airport lighting while flying overhead as this could impact other traffic.
Helicopter pilot reported he clipped the top of a road sign with his rotor blades.
Aircrew used non-standard methods to clean wing surfaces of snow.

The fuel selector for left engine malfunctioned resulting in fuel starvation of the left engine. The pilot diverted to closest field available. Poor braking action resulted in a failed tire on landing rollout.
The electric trim ran nose up with autopilot on. The aircrew overrode the system by disconnecting it.
Pilot had to take evasive action by braking heavily to avoid a ground collision with other aircraft crossing the landing runway.

Pilot drifted above cleared altitude conflicting with opposite direction traffic.  The pilot reporter corrected the error after Controller advised him of the situation. Pilot commented fatigue was a contributing factor.

An aircraft was in a Controller's sector with only a 'limited' data block displayed. The Controller did not notice the target or realize the aircraft was on their frequency and flying through their airspace.

Two N90 TRACON Controllers vectored descending/climbing aircraft for separation. One Controller believed the other Controller's aircraft would continue on a different heading than it did. The aircraft passed with less than required separation.
An aircraft on approach to SFO received incorrect glideslope information and descended below the glideslope and a crossing restriction into conflict with crossing traffic below it.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Final Approach

text: D01 TRACON Controller reported an aircraft was issued and acknowledged an instruction for a right turn missed approach. The aircraft made a left turn on their missed approach.
B737 Captain reported that the cabin altitude exceeded 10;000 feet while in climb at 25;000 feet; so he initiated an immediate descent and diverted to a nearby airport.
Captain reported that the First Officer's tablet had locked up. A Maintenance Technician corrected the problem; but did not make a logbook entry.

B737 flight crew forgot to set the flaps before taxi; but discovered the mistake during the throttle check while taxiing out. Fatigue and distractions during pushback reportedly played a role in the mistake.
Air Carrier First Officer reports the altimeters were set such that the altitude reading was higher than actual.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: Air carrier Captain reports that a lengthy ground delay and adverse winds at the destination airport required a diversion to the alternate. This resulted in landing with a low fuel state.

The Captain of a regional jet reported lining up on the wrong runway at an airport with multiple parallel runways. The error was discovered at approximately 300 feet above the ground and a missed approach was executed.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Final Approach

text: The B737 crew reported their flight took off with improper fuel loading.

A large transport aircraft flight crew pushed back from the gate and during taxi out the left main truck collapsed a steel water drainage grate. The aircraft was returned to the gate where the antiskid harness and two tires were found damaged.

Flight crew turned off beacon prior to #1 engine shutting down. Noticing the beacon was turned off; ramp personnel assumed the engines were shut down and proceeded to attempt to set out cones in front of the running engine. The Captain stated that the engine ran for 30 seconds after the start lever was placed in the cutoff position.
C182 pilot reported a taxiway incursion as well as confusion and communication issues during the interaction with ATC.

A flight instructor reported that an instrument student became disoriented due to an instrumentation problem that resulted in returning to visual conditions and a successful return to the departure airport.
show: 2016-01 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Climb

text: An IFR-certified Garmin GNC300XL installed in a C150 began giving faulty information related to courses and waypoints.
The DA20 lost power in flight so the pilots landed on a highway.
Lead pilot in a flight of four reported a runway incursion when none of the four recognized they were not actually cleared into position.

PIT Tower Controller reported of a situation where an aircraft taxied onto a closed taxiway. It appeared that he was the only one who knew the taxiway was closed and checked with Ramp Control and they did not know. Reporter wanted some type of a review of the operation because this issue with Ramp Control not knowing has been ongoing.

JCF FLM and Controller reported of a fast climbing aircraft that was out of 10;000 feet within 1-2 miles of the end of the runway. The departure was traffic for an enroute aircraft and traffic was not issued. The Departure Controller never received a rolling call. A loss of separation did occur.

A departing aircraft was issued a direct routing leaving 3;000 feet. The pilot read back the routing; but not the altitude instruction. The readback was not noticed by the controllers and the aircraft proceeded on course below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.

A departing aircraft radar data tag did not acquire on the target. The Controller did not notice and forgot about the aircraft. The adjacent sector noticed the target in their airspace and reminded the previous Controller about the aircraft.
show: 2016-01 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Climb

text: A Boeing 737 flight crew reported an inadvertent shutdown of the APU prior to the aircraft generators coming on line. This electrical system anomaly resulted in the flight management computer commanding an erroneous airspeed presentation. The crew recognized the problem and adjusted the aircraft speed and configuration accordingly.

A320 flight crew reported descending early during a visual approach to DEN resulting in a low altitude alert from Approach Control followed quickly by an EGPWS terrain warning. The flying First Officer climbed from 7;000 feet to 8;000 feet.
International Air Carrier B767 Captain reported he was concerned about the safety of his airline's operations in the far Northern routes to Europe.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Cruise
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: Air carrier flight crew entering Chinese airspace was advised by Dispatch that the weather minimums at their alternate had gone below minimums. Divert options are discussed since their destination; ZBAA; was also reporting low visibility. Dispatch advises crew it is better to declare fuel emergency than to divert as that would cause a long delay.  The crew questions the reason for having alternates that are not even useful if needed.
B757 Captain reported his iPad was not updating properly; and this is not an uncommon occurrence.
Aircraft encountered damage to the #1 engine cowl because the ground crew was unaware that the Jet Bridge was out of position when they marshaled in the aircraft.

A Boeing 737 flight crew reported experiencing severe turbulence while on an oceanic flight plan. The captain exercised emergency authority; turned off course and descended to a smoother altitude. This action was done in accordance with established overwater emergency procedures.
SF340B flight crew reported difficulty balancing fuel load in flight.
B777 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after receiving EICAS alerts RECIRC FAN and SMOKE CREW REST MAIN; followed by reports of a smoke-like odor.
show: 2016-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Wide body First Officer reported requesting a different departure from LAX when their FMC showed a wrong turn programmed on the original HOLZ9 departure.
Wide body aircraft Captain reported he had a near-collision with an SUV near his gate at MEM.
The pilot of a corporate jet reported making contact with the winglet of a parked aircraft while being marshaled on a congested ramp.
A light twin pilot and flight instructor reported a loss of control during landing that resulted in a runway excursion and damage to one propeller.

A general aviation pilot reported several encounters with vehicles operating near aircraft at Pearland Regional Airport; a privately owned airport. The pilot is concerned for the safety of all persons involved but has been unable to gain the assistance of airport management.
A flight instructor and student pilot reported on a solo landing by the student pilot that resulted in a prop strike; nose landing gear collapse; and runway excursion.
JNU Tower CIC (Controller in Charge) advised Local Control that a vehicle was approved and on the runway. Local Control argued with CIC and the aircraft departed the runway with the vehicle on it.
A flight of two aircraft departed an airport VFR and climbed head on into an inbound aircraft cleared for a Visual Approach.
DWH had one runway closed; and the pilot taxied across the departure end of an active runway.

ZID Controller and Front Line Manager (FLM) reported of an aircraft that was encountering icing conditions and had to descend. The aircraft advised ATC and started a descent below the MVA. Controller asked if the aircraft had the terrain insight and was VFR. FLM confused the Controller and the Controller then cancelled the aircraft's IFR clearance. The Controller was relieved before knowing if the aircraft landed at its destination safely.
CLT TRACON Controller was informed by a flight crew that a drone passed about 2;000 feet below the aircraft as they were climbing through 6;500 feet.
A B737 Captain reported technical problems with his ipad.
A319 flight crew reported RNAV arrival procedures; using the JAGGR STAR at DEN as an example; are increasing workload and asserted they are 'not as safe' as previous descent procedures.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: During cruise east of SLC; the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence and one Flight Attendant struck his hand on a beverage cart.

A B777 Relief Pilot at the controls and Captain resting in the bunk reported a brief; severe; turbulence jolt which injured several flight attendants. The pilots were surprised by the lack of warning and mid north latitude at which the event occurred.

The B737 crew had different indications on their flights directors and FMAs; and a steady warning horn sounded at level off. The crew returned to the departure airport; and Maintenance discovered a faulty Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU).

A distracted A321 crew quickly selected flaps 3 then landed after EGPWS alerted 'TOO LOW; FLAPS' because flaps 3 had not been selected on a manually flown visual approach with the autothrust off. Manual speed control and ILS tracking consumed the crew's attention.

A319 flight crew experienced an inadvertent go-around when the First Officer selected the expedite button while attempting to select managed speed during approach. A flap overspeed occurred before thrust could be reduced.
An A330 flight crew reported crossing the hold short line for HNL Runway 26R when they became distracted during the taxi.
B767 First Officer reported they slowly lost the center hydraulic system quantity; but landed uneventfully at their destination.

An aircraft on the Cottonwood 2 Departure from EGE turned left towards JABAN after RALPE rather than to the right to JESIE. The left turn is meant for the engine out procedure. This resulted in a conflict with ASE traffic.
Air carrier Captain reported passengers were on board the aircraft for over three hours due to a maintenance issue.
Air carrier Captain reported they encountered a brief period of severe turbulence at a reportedly smooth altitude. Three people were injured.

Air carrier Dispatcher lamented the high workloads and diminished operational control that occurs during severe weather events. Reporter suggested that the company upgrade the Dispatch work station software and bring in more dispatchers when severe weather is in the forecast.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Landing
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: Dispatcher stated that there were insufficient dispatchers to handle the workload.

A Captain in training misjudged the stop line while parking. After adding power to position the aircraft correctly he neglected to set the parking brake; causing the aircraft to roll backwards when the engines were shut down resulting in minor damage to the nose wheel steering.
The Captain was late descending for holding at PIRAT intersection because of workload.

A B737-800 Captain and his flight's Dispatcher have different opinions about applying an ice accretion weight penalty to the landing weight when ice was only encountered during climb and the Flight Operations Manual (FOM) does not provide clear guidance.
A319 flight crew landed at PSP on 31R while dealing with shifting gusty winds and a malfunctioning GPWS that gave them confusing warnings.
A passenger became ill; so the crew requested priority handling and landed at the scheduled destination. There was a wait for the medics to arrive.
A321 First Officer reported being issued numerous delay vectors based on ATC Time Based Flow Management requirements. The pilot was concerned about not being able to plan for enough fuel.
The EBBR deicing crew did not use de/anti-icing fluid on one wing of the aircraft.

The First Officer; who is a qualified Captain; flew with a high minimums Captain. They were cleared to an airport that was below high-minimums; but they were released to a nearby airport. There was confusion over call signs and flight numbers; but the weather improved and the flight landed at the intended destination uneventfully.
An A320 crew missed the SFO DYAMD TWO Arrival ARCHI NOTAM changing the ARCHI waypoint crossing restriction to 8;000 feet from the published 7;000 feet. Crew descended below SFO Class B.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: The A320 lost the yellow hydraulic system and diverted; which put them in a confusing FAR 117 situation.
B757 Captain reported problems with his iPad apps while trying to obtain company information.
B737 Captain reported he was disappointed there was no medical response team awaiting his arrival at the gate with an ill passenger even though he asked for them an hour and a half earlier.
Air carrier Captain was concerned about the removal of special qualifications for operations into SEQM.

A Dispatcher reported the difficulty he experienced when required to maintain operational control of 20 flights while concurrent training on an unfamiliar system and completing computer based training. An understaffed Dispatch during multi-airline integration was a contributing factor.
A CRJ-200 Captain reported his iPad Mini tablet Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) was difficult to use.
B767-300 Captain reported experiencing airframe buffet probably related to ice accumulation on approach to IND.
Dispatcher reported that company policy concerning fuel tankering to international destinations needed to be clarified.
The B737 Captain was task-saturated during landing rollout and did not immediately respond to taxi instructions.
A B737 First Officer reported he has observed substandard flying skills associated with Captain's from a recently merged air carrier.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: The B737 took off 100 pounds overweight due to late cargo and poor communication between Operations; Dispatch and the flight crew.

B777 flight crew reported inability to complete the Before Pushback Checklist due to a persistent fuel pressure light illumination. Maintenance was unable to correct the problem by the time the crew timed-out and the flight was cancelled.
B767 Captain reported deviating from SOP during a pushback and release procedure at an international station.
At FL350; Engine anti-ice turned off; Right Engine parameters rolled back; turned Engine anti-ice on; descended to FL250 and regained engine control.

An A320 pilot reported confusion with an MEL regarding if an Air Conditioning Pack was operational when a Class II Maintenance Message 'Pack 1 or 2' was displayed on the Centralized Fault Display System.

B757 flight crew reported an uncommanded engine acceleration while on final approach. A missed approach was initiated; the engine was shut down; and an uneventful single engine approach was accomplished.
Regional jet First Officer reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning on approach to LSE.
EMB-140 Captain reported deviating from cleared track when they were distracted by a wake vortex encounter.
show: 2016-01 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: Dash 8 Captain and an EMB-145 FO reported their near-collision on the ground when the EMB-145 experienced braking issues on black ice.

The flight crew of a business jet reported becoming disoriented while taxiing to the gate in blowing snow and low visibility conditions which resulted in the aircraft departing the paved taxiway surface.
B737-800 flight crew reported possibly exceeding tailwind limit during landing at PSP.
B737-800 flight crew reported difficulty complying with ATC taxi clearance because of slippery conditions and poor lighting.

A CRJ-200 flight crew reported nose wheel steering difficulties during taxi out. The crew associated the control issues to ice on the ground. After takeoff the gear disagree alerted with the nose wheel extended. The nose scissor link was found disconnected after landing.
show: 2016-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Climb

text: Two air carrier mechanics reported that while attempting to refuel the aircraft they discovered there was no power to the fueling panel.
The pilot of a Beech Baron reported a landing gear collapse during touchdown.
A flight instructor reported a near midair collision while providing instrument instruction to a student. Several human factors were noted by the reporter.
The pilot of a C150 reported entering a canyon that did not provide an escape route; and resulted in an off-field landing just short of the canyon rim.

A military flight instructor providing instrument instruction in a Texan II reported a controlled flight toward terrain event with a near gear overspeed when the student became overwhelmed in instrument conditions.
Light Sport Aircraft pilot reported a helicopter took off over him with about a 50 foot clearance while he was taxiing at FFZ airport.

The pilot of a general aviation aircraft reported a ground conflict at DTS; a non-towered airport; while departing on an instrument flight plan. The reporter noted that this is a recurring problem at DTS and feels that a tower is needed.
Balloon pilot reported an airspace violation due to unanticipated wind speeds.
BD700 Captain reported an NMAC with a small aircraft on departure at BFI.
The pilot flying and the non pilot flying described the circumstances that led to landing on the incorrect parallel runway at their home airport.
C182 pilot described making position reports during the arrival phase at a non-towered airport only to discover that the radio was not tuned to the correct frequency.
A C182 pilot on an instrument check flight with a flight instructor reported the loss of several electrical components; likely due to a faulty voltage regulator.
C172 pilot reported smoke and fumes from the cabin vent during takeoff that resulted in a return to the field for evaluation.
show: 2016-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Initial Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Falcon 20 flight crew reported the landing gear collapsed after landing.
C150 instructor reported engine troubles led to a forced landing in a field.

JAX TRACON Controller reported of issuing a turn to an aircraft to the right to go behind traffic. During the relief briefing; pilot reported the traffic came within 20 feet of the aircraft. Reporter said aircraft turned left instead of right.
A NORDO aircraft landed at a different airport than its flight plan destination opposite direction from the runway in use.
B767 First Officer reported they were initially dispatched on an international routing that was not authorized for their aircraft type.
B777 flight crew on an international flight reported 3 of the 4 onboard iPads were unusable following a software update. The working 4th unit was on a different software version.

After diverting due to windshear during approach at their original destination; a B747 flight crew was unable to complete all required coordination and procedures in a timely manner prior to departing the divert airport back to their original destination. The crew was given an incorrect Critical Crew Off (CCO) time prior to departing the divert airport and subsequently exceeded their FAR 117 duty day limit.
A319 Captain reported concern that the iPad mount used on the aircraft could interfere with the cockpit window operation.
Air carrier Captain reported a track deviation departing SKBO because of communication issues with ATC.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: EMB-175 Captain describes exceeding 250 knots below 10;000 FT while on descent. He mentions a new First Officer as a contributing factor for not noticing their speed.
On approach to HOU; the pilot was unable to increase his speed to accommodate faster traffic behind while remaining within stabilized approach parameters.
show: 2016-01 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: Fractional Jet flight crew experienced a close encounter with a drone while on initial approach.

The pilots of a small transport aircraft reported departing in a time pressure condition only to discover that the requested fuel load had not been added. This resulted in a return to the departure airport.
Air carrier flight crew reported procedural problems when landing north on the Runway 31's at SKBO.

Pilot reports after landing and complying with instructions to taxi from Local. Pilot switches to Ground Control and is asked why they did not contact him first and to stop. Pilot was told to make a 180 and taxi into another ramp area; wait for passing traffic; and then taxi as instructed. Pilot was confused as to what they should be doing.

The pilot of a PC-12 reported a complete loss of electrical power in instrument metrological conditions and turbulence during approach. The pilot was able to find the airport and land. The electrical system recovered on rollout. It was reported that an internal failure of the Master Power switch was the cause of the unexpected loss and recovery of the electrical system.
show: 2016-01 · Procedural: Landing Without Clearance · Initial Approach

text: The pilot of a sky diving aircraft reported a ground conflict during takeoff due to improper CTAF operations. The flight crew did not realize that the communication radio in use had the volume set very low.

CE-550 Captain; with the First Officer flying; reported a descent below the assigned altitude of 2;500 feet during approach. The First Officer had programed the autopilot to capture 2;500 feet which it did not; but he did not notice due to being fixated on the EFB.
The pilot of a PA-32 reported a main landing gear extension problem that resulted in a left main landing gear collapse during landing.
A ZMA Controller trainee passed flight estimates to another facility. The receiving facility read back one of the estimates incorrectly and it was not caught by the trainee or the instructor.

An aircraft checked on to the Controller's frequency and advised they were Non-RVSM qualified. The aircraft flight plan suffix or radar data tag did not indicate they were Non-RVSM. The controller only used 1;000 feet vertical separation between this aircraft and another one.

B737 flight crew reported executing a missed approach due to confusion over which runway was assigned to his aircraft. The confusion was attributed to ATC workload and communication issues exacerbated by radio congestion.

Air Carrier Captain reported receiving a PDC via controller pilot datalink communications (CPDLC) that does not follow standard clearance format. When queried; Clearance Deliver states that it is a new format that is an exact copy of the clearance as provided by the company. The lack of a printer with CPDLC equipped aircraft is also discussed.

Wide body captain experienced a taxiway excursion while attempting to turn from taxiway R to Taxiway C (135 degrees) at CLT. The ground is frozen and the Captain is able to continue taxiing after being checked by Maintenance.
EMB145 flight crew experienced fluctuating cabin pressure and elected to descend and divert to the nearest suitable airport.

B737-800 Captain noted a 1;000 pound fuel imbalance at the top of climb and rebalanced the fuel. During the rest of the flight the left engine consumes fuel faster than the right and a fuel leak is suspected. Upon landing a fuel leak is confirmed by Maintenance.
Wide body flight crew experienced a dual generator failure during the takeoff roll so rejected the takeoff.
Due to concerns and pressure for 'ON TIME' departures many minor maintenance items were not being worked or in many cases worked but not recorded.
Air carrier flight crew reported nose tire hit damaged area in runway surface at night during landing rollout.

B737 Captain reported two pushback events at the same airport during which different tug drivers placed the aircraft's nose gear in a jack knifed position severe enough that a more experienced ramp agent was required to reposition the aircraft properly. Poor training was cited.
B737-700 flight crew reported exiting the runway at MCI on a closed taxiway; citing confusion with the ATIS presentation as contributing.
B737 Captain reported concern with the lack of training in MEL procedures during transition classes in a new aircraft fleet.
show: 2016-01 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types · Unknown
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred All Types

text: B767-300 First Officer reported concern with deice/anti-ice procedures used on their aircraft; as well as others.
An aircraft was issued go-around instructions for two approaches in a row. The pilot felt they were too busy to read back the ATC instructions.
Air carrier Captain on downwind vectors for LAX Runway 24R near JAVSI reported a UAV near miss at approximately 5;500 - 5;700 feet.
First Officer was unable to complete approach in IMC conditions. Captain assumed flying the aircraft; executed a missed approach and landed on the second attempt at the destination airport.

A UAV presence at 300 feet on the final approach to SLC parallel runway overloaded the TRACON and disrupted communications with arriving flight crews. All associated personnel experienced workload increases.

The pilot of a corporate jet reported an increase of engine thrust while on the ramp to test the anti-ice system; then recognized that light aircraft were located relatively close behind the aircraft.
The pilot of a light twin engine aircraft reported a loss of throttle control on one engine during climb. The engine was secured and the aircraft returned to the field for a safe landing.
Embraer Legacy 450/500 pilot reported the auto flight altitude capture feature failed to level aircraft.
A multi-engine pilot in training and the flight instructor reported a near gear-up landing that resulted in damage to the propellers.
The pilot of a C182 reported diverting due to a rough running engine. After landing; it was discovered that a cylinder had failed.
The pilot of a PA-46 reported a cabin decompression; followed by a rapid descent that was not coordinated with ATC.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: The procedures in the MEL for deferring the potable water system were not accomplished completely which led up to the canceling of the flight.
S550 Pilot reported beginning his takeoff roll at LAS on a taxiway; but a call from ATC and the word 'Taxiway' on the pavement prompted him to discontinue the attempt.

The pilot of a BE-55 reported a loss of power to one engine after switching fuel tanks. After switching back to the main tank; engine did not recover; so it was feathered; followed by a successful landing.

SFO Local Controller reported that certain aircraft which taxi low to the ground have difficulty receiving transmissions in a Runway 10L dead zone along portions of Taxiways S and S2. Antenna location seems to be the problem.

An air carrier pushed from SAT Terminal A with taxi instructions N; right on G; left on Runway 4 hold short of Runway 30. Flight crew was confused; thinking his aircraft was on Taxiway N; and they taxied into the non-movement area between Taxiways G and G1 aligned with Taxiway W. Poor lighting and Taxiway N1 signage were contributing factors.
B737 flight reported taking off unknowingly with flight director switches off.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Takeoff

text: B737 flight crew reported a LAS Taxiway C incursion while taxiing around Concourse C on the ramp between Spots 11 and 10. A taxi line in that area would help maintain gate and taxiway clearance.
Once parked at the gate at SFO; crew noticed the NOTAM change to the crossing altitude at ARCHI intersection on the DYAMD 2 Arrival.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: A321 Captain reported the Additional Center Tank aft did not transfer properly. Flight diverted to interim airport.
Air carrier Captain reported they did not configure final flaps in the approach and thus executed a missed approach.
B737-800 FO reported that after an abnormal inflight fuel burn the Mechanic on the ground at the gate noticed a visible fuel leak.

CRJ-200 flight crew refused an aircraft for ferry with apparent left engine FOD damage because Company Maintenance Control gave differencing values for FAA acceptable non blended fan blade and inner wall puncture damage.
CRJ-900 flight crew was unsure if Maintenance used the proper procedure to charge the battery.
A321 flight crew reported that during descent the engine idle settings were mismatched. Flight landed in a precautionary status at the destination.
CRJ-700 First Officer reported his Electronic Flight Bag froze up multiple times on arrival in 'challenging IMC conditions'.
EMB-145 FO reported the flight crew decided to proceed to an alternate VFR when PHX TRACON shut down because of a fire.
B737 Captain reported his iPad malfunctioned in flight; leaving him without access to critical data.
Captain disagreed with de-icing crews method of cleaning snow accumulation on aircraft.
B737 First Officer reported difficulty in obtaining final weights before takeoff at MCO.
Air carrier First Officer reported the de-ice crew did not provide crew with standard information post de-ice procedure.
An ERJ-170 Captain reported that the First Officer noticed that the ground crew had loaded baggage over the forward baggage bin fire line on the previous flight.
A late change of runway in the FMC resulted in changing the cruise routing of the flight. This was at first not known to the crew. Center comments that this is a recurring event.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: G200 Captain reported intermittent loss of VHF transmit and receive capability along with EICAS indications of flight data recorder; ground/flight airbrakes; and slat/flap failures. Sufficient communication was established for approach and landing clearance to a successful no slat/flap landing.
A320 Flight Attendant reported feeling ill when the aircraft was operated over several segments with the carpet in the aft lavatory soaked from flooding.
Flight Attendant at jump seat position was struck with shards of dry ice from bag exploding.

A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports noticing an increase in the number of loose and sheared tie-bolts on B737-800 main landing gear (MLG) tire wheel-half assemblies. He recently found one tire with five tie-bolts sheared near the smooth shank and threaded portion of the tie-bolt with all the locking nuts for the tie-bolts gone.

The pilot of a C525 reported control issues suspected to be due to a trim malfunction. After returning to the field; and test of the systems; no issues were identified. The aircraft departed again with no further problems.

The pilot of a single engine Beechcraft reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC during a visual approach in MRY due to lack of familiarity with the area and distraction by the anticipated weather conditions.
A student pilot and his ground based flight instructor reported a first solo flight that resulted in the student becoming disoriented and committing an airspace violation.

PA46 Jetprop pilot learned the hard way that his 200 amp generator is limited by circuit breakers to 140 amps. During a night; IMC approach with three auxiliary failure occurs when the landing gear (50 amps) is extended. ATC provided assistance and a successful approach and landing ensues. The two main generator circuit breakers were found tripped and the electrical system functioned normally after being reset. The reporter indicates that he was never informed of the 140 amp limit in training nor is there a limitation in the POH.

A flight instructor reported that he and an instrument student experienced icing conditions while practicing instrument approaches at night in what was expected to be only marginal VFR weather. The instructor later recognized that greater safety considerations should have been taken.

A pilot reported an airborne conflict during a government contracted animal vaccine dropping flight that required grid pattern operations. Notification of the operation had not been disseminated to an associated agency.
The pilot of a C208 reported lining up for a parallel runway during a visual approach due to fatigue and distraction.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Final Approach

text: A student pilot reported a near-mid-air-collision while attempting to confirm ATC instructions which led to lining up for the incorrect parallel runway.
A helicopter pilot flying the shoreline near TOA at 100 - 300 MSL took evasive action from a UAS flying approximately 100 feet above his altitude.
A C210 pilot and flight examiner reported a landing gear extension system malfunction that occurred during a check ride; resulting in a propeller strike; go-around and return for normal landing.
The pilot of a C182 reported a descent below the glideslope on a night IFR approach; which resulted in ATC notification and go-around; followed by a successful approach and landing.

When attempting to start the engine; the pilot of a PA-28 was unaware of a tow bar connected to the nosewheel. Even though the engine did not start the propeller made contact with the tow bar. The plane was then flown in conflict with AD 2004-10-14.
Pilot reported a conflict in the pattern at PSP with a light jet due to radio interference preventing communication with PSP Tower.

An aircraft was issued a clearance to cross a fix at 14000 feet to avoid parachute jumping activity along its route at 13000 feet. The pilot readback 12000 feet. The Controller did not detect the erroneous readback.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: An aircraft responding to an RA in the traffic pattern at EDF entered the MRI Class D airspace without clearance.
show: 2016-01 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: Air carrier flight crew and Controller reported of confusion related to Descend Via clearance. Controller issued descend via the JOVEM2 STAR at least twice. Pilot had received from previous Controller descend via the STAR except maintain 6;000 feet. Controller thought the last clearance he issued was the one the pilot should have done. Pilots were confused and did not do what the last instruction from ATC was.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: Air crew was not able to see cleared taxiway exit point off of runway during landing rollout due to snow conditions.
Air Carrier flight crew reported the nose gear was damaged when it was struck by the pushback tug.
B737-700 FO reported the PAPI lights for 24R at LAX appear to be designed for a displaced threshold that is not yet being used.
show: 2016-01 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: B737-800 flight crew reported experiencing a tail strike on takeoff in gusty winds at TPA.
B737-700 FO reported the Captain; as the pilot flying; chose to use CRZ DESC mode rather than VNAV; and was having difficulty complying with the RNAV STAR constraints.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: B767 Captain questioned the de-ice crew procedure to not deice the fuselage top; their piecemeal deice procedure; and reluctance to deice any surface other than flight control surfaces. The Captain directed all ice and icicles be removed.
EMB-505 Captain reported diverting to a nearby alternate after a precautionary shutdown of the #1 engine because of a bleed leak.
CRJ-700 Captain reported a track deviation on approach when the flying pilot First Officer selected green needles too soon.
show: 2016-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: Air carrier Captain commented that CRW Runway 5 is a black hole following a landslide which disabled the ILS Glideslope; VASI; and REIL while displacing the runway threshold.

B737 First Officer believes that his flight to MUGM may have entered Cuban airspace at an inappropriate altitude since Cuban AFS for military protocol requires flights to be conducted under VFR denying them of altitude at or above FL180.
Light twin pilot on an IFR flight plan in VMC reported descending to 4;500 feet from 5;000 feet after several attempts to cancel IFR with ATC.
show: 2016-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: PA28 pilot reports hitting something with the left wing tip just after takeoff from a dirt road on BLM land. The aircraft is flown back to home base without incident.
FXE Tower Controller reported a recurring problem with coyotes. An aircraft was issued a go-around due to a coyote on the runway. A landing aircraft reported almost hitting a coyote on the runway.
show: 2016-01 · Ground: Person / Animal / Bird · Final Approach

text: B737 Captain described the confusion created when a deice crew failed to utilize the standardized communications before; during; and after deicing his aircraft. The process nearly resulted in a ground collision with a deice vehicle.
B737-700 flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate after receiving a Cabin Altitude Warning.
During approach to BZN; aircrew experienced a GPWS terrain warning and executed the escape maneuver.
A B777 First Officer described his company's inhospitable crew rest bunk conditions which are not conducive to sleep and result in flight crew fatigue during the flight's final stages.
Aircraft experienced failure of the attitude and heading reference system resulting in multiple failures in flight dynamic subsystems.

text: B737 flight crew reported MEL fueling procedures at Contract Maintenance location may have countered company policy.

Air carrier First Officer reported being distracted during takeoff roll by a bird which emerged from inside the cockpit. Aircraft control was maintained at all times and the bird subsequently disappeared for the remainder of the flight.

Flight Attendant reported a passenger illness which a passenger physician diagnosed as a heart attack. O2 was administered and Automatic Electronic Defibrillator (AED) monitored heart rhythms until paramedics removed ill passenger.

The pilot of a C150 reported loss of engine power due to suspected carb ice. After regaining engine power; the flight was successfully completed. The pilot noted the need for more awareness to carb ice conditions and more aggressive use of carb heat.
CRJ-900 torque links on nose gear were not secured after towing. Aircraft lost nose wheel steering upon landing.
The pilot of a PA-34 reported a nose landing gear collapse; propeller strike; and runway excursion occurred during a check ride after landing flat on all 3 tires.

During night-time taxi to Runway 33 at BUR; crew crossed the hold short line. The Airport Diagram (BUR 10-9) was changed just four days after this incident to add a Hot Spot and related note for this spot on the airport.
Air carrier Captain reported a misunderstanding between the Captain and First Officer whether to fly runway heading or comply with the RNAV Departure procedures which resulted in heading deviation.

text: B737NG flight crew reported a runway incursion at 31R in MDW.

Air carrier flight crew experienced non-standard procedures from ground personnel while parking aircraft at SFO gate.
A300 flight crew experienced heating brake indications after takeoff. Brakes eventually cooled; so flight crew landed at the destination in a precautionary emergency status.
EMB-145LR Captain reported diverting to a nearby alternate after losing the air/ground sensor in flight.
B737NG flight crew reported getting low during a night visual approach to Runway 36R at TUL. A single EGPWS 'obstacle' alert was annunciated and the flying First Officer executed a go around.
Air carrier flight crew executed a rejected takeoff after seeing a vehicle on the departure runway.
CRJ-200 Captain forgot to turn off the Nose Gear Steering when the ground crew connected the tow bar and attempted to push back the aircraft from the gate.

The airport self-parking system recognizes an incoming aircraft as an obstruction; therefore; the 'STOP-OBSTRUCTION' feature of the system is no longer functional; so if there is a truck or an object in the envelope that may potentially cause damage to the aircraft; the self-parking system will not recognize it.
MD80 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff at a low speed when they received a takeoff warning horn related to flap setting.

CRJ-200 Flight Crew and the Dispatcher involved described a taxiway excursion during exit from the runway after landing. The braking action for the runway had been reported as good on packed snow but the nose wheel steering was ineffective during exit from the runway and braking action was nil.
B737-700 Captain reported he deliberately overshot his level off altitude because he was dealing with moderate turbulence and was concerned about an overspeed.

B767-400 flight crew departing Runway 33 was cleared for a left turn after takeoff heading 110; which was set in the MCP. Once airborne heading select was called for and a right turn initiated to follow the flight director. ATC detected the error and corrected the turn direction. The flying First Officer had little actual flying experience in the B767-400; with its altitude and speed tape difference from the rest of the fleet.

A Ground Security Coordinator was sent out and after a full security search the aircraft was reboarded.

text: B737 flight crew reported an NMAC with a light aircraft on arrival into EWR.

On the right downwind segment of a visual approach to RDU Runway 5L; crew commenced base-leg turn in response to an ATC inquiry. In the turn the crew received a GPWS obstacle warning and a low-altitude alert from ATC simultaneously. Crew followed the EGPWS guidance and returned to a normal approach and landing.

During a repositioning flight; the flight crew was asked to an Operational Check Flight (OCF) and deploy the Air Driven Generator (ADG). There was some confusion weather the flight was dispatched properly.
B737-800 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff when they received a LE FLAPS TRNSIT warning at approximately 90 KTS.

Challenger 600 crew arriving at aircraft found the AC external power door closed and partially latched. Closing the door moves an internal switch to the 'close' position so when hydraulic pressure is reapplied the nose doors close. A dangerous situation if any ground personnel are nearby. The external power door should be left open.
The A319 Captain reported that the parking system is slow to respond conflicting ground traffic in the Safety Zone.

A320 Captain reported discovering during the Before Start Checklist that the fuel load was 1;000 pounds less than their release. Research revealed that Load Planning made the change on their own to accommodate more passengers and cargo.
A320 FO reported the Captain landed on the displaced threshold of Runway 22R at EWR even after the FO warned against that.
EC-130 pilot reported departing with the fuel cap off.
The C400 First Officer reported that an engine ran rough in flight and then both engines shut off after landing.
B787 flight crew reported stabilizer trim failure on descent. Crew followed procedure and landed uneventfully.

A300 flight crew experienced a windshear warning at 800 feet during visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ with strong gusty winds reported. The Captain elects not to go around and the First Officer is not forceful in suggesting that he should. The windshear warning stops after two announcements and a normal landing ensues.
On the approach to LAX; the First Officer was high and fast; but was stable by 500 feet.
The CRJ-200 First Officer reported on a duct warning that led the crew to land at the nearest suitable airport.
Passengers started boarding before the flight attendants were ready for them.
Flight Attendant describes new larger overhead bins are harder to close due to the larger amount of weight they are designed to carry.
CRJ-900 Flight Attendant reported difficulty safely exiting the aircraft because of the steep jet bridge extension angle.

B757 Captain refused an aircraft because of uncertainty about the integrity of the entertainment system wiring that could possibly pose a fire hazard.
Air carrier flight crew reported climbing through a crossing restriction departing RJAA with distractions from windshear or a wake vortex encounter playing a part.
B777 international First Officer reported the entire crew had issues with their iPad usability and availability for the long-range transoceanic round trip.

A mechanic lost control of an aircraft while pushing aircraft out of the hangar onto an icy ramp area. The tug slid under and engine cowl and broke off drain mast.
The pilot reported on his encounter with a street lamp after landing his hot air balloon.

Q400 Captain reported he was on short final to SEA Runway 16L when he heard Tower clear another aircraft to cross the runway. Tower cancelled that clearance after a heads-up from the reporter.

SLC Tower Controller reported that he was distracted and almost let an aircraft land on a closed runway. The Controller did not use memory joggers to remind him of the closure. The AMASS alerted along with another Controller advising him. The aircraft was sent around and landed on an open runway.

HUF Tower Controller reported they had a shift where the facility was short staffed; problems with a flight school; and an aircraft that was told to exit at a specific taxiway; but exited at a different taxiway due to its speed. Controller thought he might have to send aircraft on final around; but did not have to because the aircraft made a full stop landing when cleared for the option.

ZJX Controller reported another facility handed off an aircraft to him. The Controller then sees a target in the warning area climbing towards the aircraft just handed off. Controller issued traffic and called the other facility.  Other facility stated aircraft is restricted to a specific altitude. Aircraft busted altitude and buzzed the aircraft just handed off. Controller reported the violation to the other facility.

text: ZAU ARTCC Controller reported an aircraft with pressurization issues was vectored and descended into a TRACON's airspace without proper coordination.

JFK Local Controller reported an aircraft turned to exit the runway at a closed and blocked intersection. The next arrival had to be sent around. In the go around the aircraft now became a conflict for two other aircraft. Eventually the go around traffic comes back and lands. Controller reported that he thought the Port Authority should have done a better job clearing the intersections from snow.

SMO Developmental Tower Controller reported of issuing instructions to a helicopter. The aircraft did not fly as instructed and became a conflict for arrival traffic. Instructing Controller turned the helicopter to avoid the arrival. Arrival aircraft reported an RA and advised Tower they had the aircraft in sight.

DCA Tower Controller reported a landing aircraft attempted to exit the runway at the wrong intersection. The delay caused an arrival to be issued go-around instructions. The Local Controller failed to issue traffic to two VFR helicopters; one of which took evasive action.
Tower Controller reported an aircraft did not comply with taxi instructions and proceeded onto a runway another aircraft was landing on.

TPA TRACON Controller reported of losing a data block along with the primary target. The aircraft was in conflict with the downwind traffic. Reporter advised the FLM; who told him this had happened several times before he took the position. Controller would like this looked into to avoid it from happening again.
ZME ARTCC Controller reported a VFR aircraft encountering IMC weather was assisted by ATC to a safe landing. The brasher warning was issued to the pilot as assistance was being provided.
A BHM Tower Local Controller did not slow an aircraft following a slower aircraft on final approach in a timely manner. The first aircraft had to be issued go-around instructions.

HWD Tower Controller reported of Class Delta airspace violation.  The Controller working the Approach Control position was called by HWD Tower Controller and asked about the violating aircraft. Converging traffic was being worked by the Tower Controller. Overlying TRACON Controller never asked for a point out or advised that visual separation was being used.

The B737 crew reported on a mistake in the performance calculations because of a deferred performance computer and an incorrect entry of Zero Fuel Weight instead of Takeoff gross Weight.

Two aircraft in a CTAF environment conflicted during an approach and departure in IMC conditions.

The SJC TECKY TWO Departure has a speed restriction of at or below 230 KIAS; which is misleading as it is below the SFO Class B Airspace with a limit of 200 KIAS.
PA-34 Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at DTO.
PA-20 pilot operating on skis lost directional control on the icy surface while clearing the runway and struck a runway edge light.

Turning the hydraulic pump back on the aircraft 'jerked' indicating pressure; but the tendency to roll remained.

text: Dispatcher reported on crew communication difficulties regarding fuel loads on an international flight.
SA-227AC Captain reported experiencing a brake fire during an extended taxi with nosewheel steering inoperative.
Concerned about icing; the pilot may have deviated from his assigned altitude after a missed approach at ANE.
ZOB Controller lost their main radio transmitters. The Controller was working two aircraft head on at the same altitude. Both aircraft responded to TCAS/RA alerts.

Two aircraft were on approach to parallel runways. ATC placed an aircraft on the left runway to line up and wait. The arriving aircraft on the right runway initiated a go-around for an RA on the aircraft landing on the left runway. The departing aircraft did not depart in a timely manner so the arrival for the left runway was issued a go-around by Tower.

Due to a radar outage; K90 TRACON was receiving their radar information from ZBW ARTCC. The ARTCC has to make a data entry of the current altimeter for the TRACON airspace yet the ARTCC did not realize this requirement. Therefore the Mode C readouts of aircraft in the TRACON airspace were 400 feet off from the actual altitude of the aircraft.

PCT Controller reported of a loss of separation resulting from a speed overtake. Controller was also training at the time and attempted to have the Developmental fix the situation. Reporter then confronted the transferring Controller who said it was not his fault and that the aircraft were separated when he shipped them.

The Local Controller did not notice an aircraft entering downwind was in close proximity to another aircraft already on downwind. Due to workload the Controller had requested an assist position to help them but the request was denied.

ZKC Developmental reported of releasing an aircraft off of a controlled airport and not getting radar contact on it until 24 minutes after it departed. This aircraft also violated another Approach Control's airspace. Procedure to call reporting the aircraft as rolling or departing; is reportedly not being followed.

B737-800 Captain reported a large amount of grease around the landing gears and in the E&E compartment left over after midnight maintenance serviced the aircraft.

B737 flight crew reported receiving an RA from a nearby regional jet on parallel approaches to SFO Runways 28L and 28R.

A C150 Instructor conducting a checkout with a licensed pilot failed to select carburetor heat during stall training which resulted in the engine quitting. A successful off airport landing followed unsuccessful inflight start attempts.

text: A Captain called off a trip fatigued on the third day after two nights of sleep deficit at hotels where late loud noise interfered with rest opportunities.

A crew departed the BOS North Cargo Ramp with clearance to Taxiway B via Taxiway L but turned left after leaving the Cargo Ramp and taxied via the General Aviation Ramp to Taxiway B. The event occurred during night conditions with snow. More accurate North Cargo airport charting was suggested.

EMB-145 crew deiced at the gate with the APU running. Immediately after takeoff; the cabin and cockpit filled with smoke and the flight returned to the departure airport. Deice fluid was suspected as the smoke's source.

text: A fatigued air taxi crew transitioning from the LAS GRNPA 1 RNAV Arrival to a night visual mistook HND for LAS and descended below the MSA before ATC alerted.

CE560 flight crew experienced a strong rolling tendency and aileron trim binding during initial climb then the controls are passed to the PIC in the right seat. The crew elects to return to the departure airport and the PIC is able to adjust the aileron trim to neutralize the rolling tendency prior to landing.
A pilot on a photo mission talking to ATC felt they might have entered Class B Airspace without ATC clearing them into it.
Alien private pilot starting an instrument training course asked his instructor if a new TSA alien form was required and was told no. This proved to be incorrect.
C172 instructor pilot reported loss of directional control after landing when the left brake failed.
A319 First Officer pointed out to ATC that on his route there were two waypoints with similar spelling and identical pronunciation; LYNDE and LYNDI.
C310 pilot reported an NMAC at 9;000 FT while on an IFR flight.

G280 First Officer described a track deviation when the Captain (pilot monitoring) attempted to program the FMC with a crossing restriction while talking to ATC. Somehow the FMC is sequenced to the next fix and the aircraft turns early. The Captain is unwilling to advise ATC of the FMC issues and request a vector.
