text: Air carrier First Officer reported a taxi deviation at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport (ZGSZ). He attributed the error to several ambiguous taxiway markings at this airport.
C172 flight instructor reported striking a runway threshold light during landing with his student at the controls.

GA pilot experienced an airborne conflict with another aircraft that had announced entering the pattern for Runway 20; but wound up on approach to Runway 02 in conflict with the reporter. Evasive action was taken by the reporter and the NORDO pilot departed to the south without making radio contact.
A B737 First Officer reported taxiing the aircraft for departure prior to having the flaps set for takeoff.
A B737 Captain reported missing an altitude restriction due to an FMC programming error and distractions caused by ACARS problems.

A Ramp Agent installed a tow bar between loading baggage tasks but failed to install the nose gear steering bypass pin. The tow bar separated from the nose wheel then rolled 6 to 8 feet after the agent notified the crew. Maintenance found no damage so connected a new tow bar to resume the push.
B757-200 flight crew reported an EICAS 'LE SLAT DIS' message while on approach.

CRJ-700 Captain at 12;000 feet experienced a TCAS RA with a small aircraft 500 feet below. The TCAS commanded a Climb Climb then an 'Increase climb'; followed quickly by 'Descend; Descend.'  In the end it appeared that the light aircraft had never changed altitude.

Embraer jet Captain reported that while above the RNAV flight path angle to ROA Runway 24; the GPWS erroneously alerted a single 'TERRAIN; TERRAIN' as the landing gear was lowered. The reporter also described the exceptionally dim MFD terrain display.

HS-125 flight crew experienced pitot static system malfunctions shortly after takeoff and returned to the departure airport. None of the airspeed indicators appeared to be functioning normally and AOA was used for the approach.
A First Officer of an A320 reported his concern about the application of an MEL procedure for engine anti-ice.
An Embraer ERJ-175 Captain reported they returned to the gate due to an intoxicated/ill passenger.

The flight crews of a B737 and an A320 series aircraft reported their winglets made contact as both aircraft were pushed back from adjacent jetways. Normal ramp tower conflict advisory instructions had not been issued and the ground crew actions are not known.
Captain of a medium sized turbojet reported that the proximity and arrangement of a taxiway makes it appear as if taxiing traffic is on runway 27R.
A Boeing 737 Flight Attendant reported the cockpit door closed before she could get in to relieve the First Officer for a lav break.
A Bombardier Challenger 650 Maintenance Technician reported that there is some confusion identifying a required inspection item for the fuel system.
Captain of a large passenger turbojet reported experiencing a failure of one IRS system which inhibited their ability to enter ETOPS airspace.
DA20 student pilot and the observing CFI reported that upon landing during a solo flight the aircraft turned sharply and departed the runway.
PA28 pilot reported a NMAC with a UAV at 3500 MSL in the vicinity of DFW.
Beechcraft A36 pilot reported a landing gear collapse upon landing.  The previous day; the pilot reported that the aircraft had gear issues.
SAT Tower Controller reported an aircraft on short final initiated a go-around due to departing traffic from the same runway.
ZDV Center Controller observed a VFR parachute jump aircraft climb through the altitude of an enroute IFR aircraft that the VFR aircraft had been advised of.
SCT TRACON Controller reported STARS or Fusion radar erroneously displayed a target which caused a fake conflict with a SNA arrival.
A Center Controller observed a diverting aircraft with an alternator problem descend without a clearance to an altitude below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
A Boeing 737 Flight Crew reported that they discovered the fuel distribution for the aircrat was not correct.
B737 flight crew reported that the First Officer experienced erroneous airspeed indications while flying through heavy rain.
A319 Captain refused the assigned aircraft due to inoperative lav.
B737NG Captain reported he continued to destination after experiencing high battery amperage. Problem was later traced to amp gauge wiring.
B777 flight crew of a large passenger turbojet reported an issue after takeoff of unsecured cargo pallets. Flight diverted to fix the issue then continued on to its original destination.

B737 Captain reported while the aircraft was being refueled in SFO the fueler did not have the static line attached because it was broken. Captain reported having a mechanic repair the static line; so fueling could be completed.
B757 Captain reported concern regarding company policy regarding cell phones which are lost/left on aircraft and not recovered before the aircraft is dispatched for subsequent flights.

EMB-145 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff and returning to the gate for maintenance after experiencing nose wheel steering issues.

The First Officer of an medium size air carrier aircraft reported they received an EICAS message indicating a 'Spoiler Failure'.
CE-560EP Captain reported receiving a false GPWS terrain warning on climb out from FHR; presumably related to a database error.
The Captain of an Embraer reported that after push-back the nose wheel was completely turned around.
Air carrier Captain reported that after landing in SKBO he noted differences between taxiway designations and their charting.
A300 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff and returning for maintenance after experiencing anomalies affecting both generators. The problem was traced to water in the avionics compartment.

CRJ700 flight crew and Flight Attendant reported changes to their takeoff clearance distracted the flight crew and caused them to takeoff before completing checklists and alerting the Flight Attendants.
